In this scenario, the taxpayer's property is a personal residence because it was rented for 10 days. The rental income is excluded from income, and the rental expenses are not deductible. Had the property been rented for more than 14 days, it would be considered a vacation home, and $7,500 of rental income would be taxable ("$7,500").
questions.explanationJa: 私的にも使う住宅の賃貸は、賃貸日数によって扱いが変わる。年14日以下の賃貸であればその住宅は自宅（personal residence）として扱われ、賃貸収入は総所得から除外され、広告費・手数料などの賃貸費用も控除できない。本問は10日間の賃貸なので、報告する純賃貸収入は$0である。14日超の賃貸であれば別荘扱いとなり、$7,500（$10,000－$1,000－$500－$1,000）が課税されていた。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.59

questions.stem:
A taxpayer travels once a month to an out-of-state casino. In Year 4, the taxpayer's expenses and earnings relating to gambling were as follows:

Transportation costs to and from casinos | $1,200
Lodging at casinos | $1,500
Cost of wagers | $20,000
Gambling winnings | $30,000

The taxpayer is not considered a professional gambler. What is the taxpayer's allowed deduction related to gambling for Year 4?
questions.explanation:
Gambling losses are deductible as an itemized deduction to the extent of winnings ("$0"). Gambling winnings are reported separately in income on Form 1040. The gambling losses are not netted against the winnings. Excess losses may not be carried over.

The deduction for expenses associated with gambling also is allowed for any individual taxpayer (not just professionals). These expenses include travel, lodging, and meals. However, the total deduction is limited to the amount of the gambling winnings.

In this scenario, all the expenses are deductible because their total amount is less than the $30,000 in gambling winnings. Therefore, the taxpayer's deduction relating to gambling for Year 4 is $22,700 ($1,200 + $1,500 + $20,000).
questions.explanationJa: ギャンブルの賞金は総所得に計上し、損失はそれと相殺せず、賞金の額を限度として項目別控除に計上する。限度を超えた損失は繰り越せない。出典の解説によれば、ギャンブルに伴う交通費・宿泊費などの費用も、職業ギャンブラーに限らず賞金の範囲内で控除できる。本問の費用合計は賞金$30,000を下回るため全額控除でき、控除額は$22,700（$1,200＋$1,500＋$20,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.60

questions.stem: The income or loss resulting from which of the following activities is most likely to be considered passive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Annuity income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Year-end bonus received by an employee for outstanding performance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gain from sale of a trademarked advertising slogan realized by the creator of the slogan.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Income allocated to a silent partner in a general partnership that owns and operates laundromats.

questions.explanation:
There are two sources for passive income: (1) all rental activities (exception for real estate professionals), or (2) a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate (partnerships, S corporations). Passive income generally includes gains from disposition of an interest or property used in a passive activity. Passive activity losses are only deductible to the extent of passive income (except for rental real estate professionals).

A taxpayer who is a silent partner in a general partnership that owns and operates laundromats is an example of a passive activity from a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate. Any income or loss received from the partnership is considered passive.

("Annuity income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or busin…") Annuity income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business is classified as portfolio income, not passive income.

("Year-end bonus received by an employee for outstanding performance.") A year-end bonus received by an employee is considered wages, which is active, not passive, income.

("Gain from sale of a trademarked advertising slogan realized by the cr…") If the taxpayer's personal efforts significantly contributed to the creation of intangible property, the income (gain from sale of a trademarked advertising slogan realized by the creator) is considered active, not passive.
questions.explanationJa: パッシブ所得の源泉は、すべての賃貸活動（不動産専門家を除く）と、実質的に関与していない事業（パートナーシップ、S corporation）である。洗濯店を経営するゼネラル・パートナーシップの匿名組合員（silent partner）は、実質的に関与していない事業の典型例なので、その配分所得はパッシブとなる。通常の事業から生じたものでない年金所得はポートフォリオ所得、従業員の賞与は給与として能動的所得である。自ら考案した広告スローガンの商標の売却益も、本人の努力で生み出した無形資産からの所得なので能動的所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.61

questions.stem: An individual taxpayer received rental income from real estate that was rented below market value to a not-for-profit organization. On what form should the rental income be reported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Schedule C.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Schedule E.

choices.label: C
choices.text: None since the income was earned from a not-for-profit organization and is tax exempt.

choices.label: D
choices.text: None since rental income is reported as a line item on Form 1040.

questions.explanation:
Only the net income or loss from the rental activity should be reported on Form 1040 ("None since rental income is reported as a line item on Form 1040."). Rental income and associated expenses should be detailed on Schedule E. Schedule E also is used to report income and expenses from royalty and pass-through activities.

("Schedule C.") Schedule C is used to report detailed income and expenses from businesses operated as sole proprietorships.

("None since the income was earned from a not-for-profit organization a…") The rental income is taxable even if the rent is below market and received from a tax-exempt entity. The amount of rent and tax status of the renter are irrelevant. The renter is tax-exempt, not the landlord.
questions.explanationJa: 賃貸収入とそれに関連する費用はSchedule Eに記載し、純損益だけをForm 1040に記載する。家賃が市場価格を下回っていても、借り手が非営利の免税団体であっても、免税となるのは借り手であって貸し手ではないため、賃貸収入は課税される。Schedule Cは個人事業の損益を報告する様式である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.62

questions.stem:
Married taxpayers are filing a joint income tax return. They derive their entire income from the operation of their retail candy shop. Their Year 1 AGI was $50,000. The taxpayers itemized their deductions on Schedule A for Year 1. The following unreimbursed cash expenditures were among those made by the taxpayers during Year 1:

State income tax | $1,200
Self-employment tax | 7,650

What amount should the taxpayers deduct for taxes in their itemized deductions on Schedule A for Year 1?
questions.explanation:
In general, taxpayers who elect to take itemized deductions may deduct certain nonbusiness (personal) taxes on Form 1040, Schedule A. All taxes that qualify as itemized deductions must have been paid during the tax year. Property taxes must be for property located in the U.S. These taxes consist of:

State and local personal property taxes. The tax must be based on the property's value. Standard fees (processing fee) are not deductible

State and local real estate property taxes. The taxpayer must own the property. Deductions for foreign real property taxes are not allowed for 2018 through 2025

State and local income taxes or sales taxes. Taxpayers can elect to deduct one or the other but not both

Foreign income taxes. These can be claimed as a tax credit or a deduction but not both

The deduction for state and local income and property taxes paid is limited to a total of $10,000 ($5,000 for married taxpayers filing separate returns) for 2018 through 2025.

In this scenario, the taxpayers should deduct only the $1,200 state income tax as an itemized deduction on Schedule A for Year 1.

("$3,825" / "$5,025" / "$7,650") All of these choices incorrectly include some or all of the self-employment tax. One-half of self-employment tax qualifies as a deduction from gross income (deducted for calculating AGI) but is not an itemized deduction.
questions.explanationJa: 項目別控除を選んだ納税者は、当年に支払った一定の個人的な税金（州・地方の財産税、州・地方の所得税または売上税、外国所得税など）をSchedule Aで控除できる。州・地方の所得税と財産税の控除は合計$10,000（夫婦個別申告は$5,000）が上限である。本問でSchedule Aに計上するのは州所得税$1,200だけである。自営業税は、その2分の1がAGI計算前の控除となるだけで、項目別控除にはならない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.63

questions.stem: A taxpayer filed an income tax return after the due date but neglected to file an extension form. The return indicated a tax liability of $50,000 and taxes withheld of $45,000. What amount, if any, would be used to compute the penalties for late filing and late payment?
questions.explanation:
A taxpayer who files a late tax return and underpays the taxes due is subject to both penalties--late filing and late payment. Both penalties are calculated as a percentage of the unpaid taxes. The taxpayer paid $45,000 in taxes through withholding. Total taxes due were $50,000. Therefore, the amount of unpaid taxes is $5,000, which is the amount used to calculate both penalties.

("$0") The question indicates a $5,000 underpayment. If the taxpayer had paid all the tax due, or there was an overpayment, then $0 would be correct.

("$45,000") The amount of $45,000 incorrectly assumes the penalties are based on the total taxes paid instead of the total unpaid taxes. Note that withheld taxes are considered paid by the taxpayer even though they aren't remitted with the taxpayer's filed tax return.

("$50,000") The amount of $50,000 incorrectly assumes the penalties are based on the total taxes due instead of the total unpaid taxes.
questions.explanationJa: 期限後申告で納税不足もある場合は、期限後申告と期限後納付の両方のペナルティが課され、いずれも未納税額に対する割合で計算される。源泉徴収された税額は申告書と一緒に納めていなくても納付済みとして扱われる。したがって両ペナルティの計算基礎は未納額の$5,000（税額$50,000－源泉徴収$45,000）である。納付済み税額$45,000や税額全体$50,000を基礎にするのは誤りである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.64

questions.stem: Alex, a CPA, provided accounting services to a client, Bailey. On December 15, Bailey gave Alex 100 shares of publicly traded stock as compensation for services. The adjusted basis of the stock was $4,000, and its fair market value at the time of transfer was $5,000. On February 15, Alex sold the stock for $7,500. What is the amount that Alex should recognize as gain on the sale of stock?
questions.explanation: when the taxpayer is paid with noncash property, the amount to report as income is the fair market value (FMV) of the property or services received. Alex recognized $5,000 of income when the stock was received. Alex assumed a $5,000 basis in the stock. When the stock was sold, Alex recognized a $2,500 gain ($7,500 − $5,000).
questions.explanationJa: 非金銭的財産で報酬を受け取った場合、その財産の公正市場価値を所得として計上する。Alexは株式の受取時に時価$5,000を所得に計上し、これが株式の取得原価となる（顧客側の取得原価$4,000は関係しない）。したがって売却時に認識する利得は$2,500（$7,500－$5,000）である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.65

questions.stem: Jefferson's investment income consisted of $2,000 in interest from a U.S. Treasury bond and $1,000 interest from a municipal bond. Jefferson also paid $4,000 in investment interest expense. Assuming that Jefferson itemizes, what amount can Jefferson deduct for investment interest expense?
questions.explanation: In this scenario, Jefferson has $2,000 of investment income. The municipal bond interest of $1,000 is tax exempt and thus not included in investment income. There are no investment expenses other than interest. The deduction for investment interest expense ($4,000) is limited to the lesser of TII $2,000 or interest expense ($4,000)
questions.explanationJa: 投資利子費用の控除額は、支払った投資利子と課税対象の投資所得のいずれか少ない額に限られる。米国財務省債券の利子$2,000は投資所得に含まれるが、地方債の利子$1,000は非課税なので投資所得に含まれない。投資利子以外の投資費用はないため、控除額は投資利子$4,000と投資所得$2,000の少ない方の$2,000である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG Individual Taxation Q.66

questions.stem: A married couple purchased their principal residence for $300,000. They spent $40,000 on improvements. After living in it for 10 years, the couple sold the home for $650,000 and paid $36,000 in real estate commissions. What gain should the couple recognize on their joint return?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §121, a married couple filing jointly may exclude up to $500,000 of gain on the sale of a principal residence they owned and used as their principal residence for at least two of the five years before the sale. The couple lived in the home for 10 years.

Amount realized = $650,000 - $36,000 commissions = $614,000
Adjusted basis = $300,000 + $40,000 improvements = $340,000
Realized gain = $614,000 - $340,000 = $274,000
Excluded gain = $274,000 (within the $500,000 limit)
Recognized gain = $0

The $274,000 amount is the realized gain before applying the §121 exclusion.
The $310,000 amount ignores the selling commissions and also fails to apply the exclusion.
The $60,000 amount has no basis in the exclusion rules; the entire gain is within the $500,000 limit for a joint return.
questions.explanationJa:
主たる住居を売却した場合、売却前5年のうち2年以上所有・居住していれば、夫婦合算申告では $500,000 まで譲渡益を非課税にできる（IRC §121）。
実現額 = $650,000 − 手数料 $36,000 = $614,000、取得価額 = $300,000 + 改良費 $40,000 = $340,000、譲渡益 = $274,000。全額が $500,000 の範囲内なので認識する利益は $0。
$274,000 は除外前の譲渡益。$310,000 は手数料を差し引かず除外も適用していない。$60,000 は根拠が無く、利益全額が除外の範囲内にある。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 9952)

questions.stem: Doyle has gambling losses totaling $7,000 during the current year. Doyle's adjusted gross income is $60,000, including $3,000 in gambling winnings. Doyle can itemize the deductions. What amount of gambling losses is deductible?
questions.explanation:
Gambling losses are an itemized deduction allowed only to the extent of gambling winnings (IRC §165(d)). For tax years beginning after December 31, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act limits the deductible amount to 90% of wagering losses, still capped at wagering gains.

90% of losses = $7,000 x 90% = $6,300
Limited to gambling winnings of $3,000
Deductible gambling losses = $3,000

The $0 amount is incorrect because a taxpayer who itemizes may deduct gambling losses up to winnings.
The $5,800 amount has no basis in the gambling loss rules; gambling losses are not subject to an AGI floor.
The $7,000 amount ignores the limitation to gambling winnings.
questions.explanationJa:
ギャンブルの損失は、ギャンブルの所得（勝ち金）の範囲内でのみ項目別控除として控除できる（IRC §165(d)）。2026年以降開始の課税年度は OBBBA により損失の90%が対象となるが、勝ち金を上限とする点は変わらない。
損失の90% = $7,000 × 90% = $6,300、勝ち金 $3,000 が上限 → 控除額 $3,000。
$0 は、項目別控除を選べば勝ち金まで控除できるので誤り。$5,800 には根拠が無い（AGI に連動する足切りは無い）。$7,000 は勝ち金による上限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.15 (AICPA No. 9955)

questions.stem: Sam's year 2 taxable income was $175,000 with a corresponding tax liability of $30,000. For year 3, Sam expects taxable income of $250,000 and a tax liability of $50,000. In order to avoid a penalty for underpayment of estimated tax, what is the minimum amount of year 3 estimated tax payments that Sam can make?
questions.explanation:
To avoid the underpayment of estimated tax penalty (IRC §6654(d)(1)), an individual's required annual payment is the lesser of (1) 90% of the current-year tax or (2) 100% of the prior-year tax. If the prior-year AGI exceeded $150,000, the prior-year percentage is 110% (IRC §6654(d)(1)). Sam's year 2 taxable income was $175,000, so his year 2 AGI was at least $175,000 and exceeded $150,000.

90% of year 3 tax = $50,000 x 90% = $45,000
110% of year 2 tax = $30,000 x 110% = $33,000
Minimum required payments = lesser amount = $33,000

The $30,000 amount uses 100% of the prior-year tax, which applies only when prior-year AGI is $150,000 or less.
The $45,000 amount is 90% of the current-year tax, which is larger than the prior-year safe harbor.
The $50,000 amount is the entire current-year tax.
questions.explanationJa:
予定納税の過少納付ペナルティを避けるには、①当年税額の90% と ②前年税額の100%（前年AGIが $150,000 超なら110%）のいずれか少ない額を納付すればよい（IRC §6654(d)）。前年の課税所得が $175,000 なので前年AGIも $150,000 を超える。
当年税額の90% = $45,000、前年税額の110% = $33,000 → 少ない方の $33,000。
$30,000 は前年税額の100%で、前年AGIが $150,000 以下のときの基準。$45,000 は当年基準で多い方。$50,000 は当年税額の全額。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.29 (AICPA No. 9969)

questions.stem:
In the current year, a taxpayer reports the following items. The taxpayer materially participates in partnership A.

Salary | $50,000
Income from partnership A | 20,000
Passive activity loss from partnership B | (40,000)

During the year, the taxpayer disposed of the interest in partnership B, which had a suspended loss carryover of $10,000 from prior years. What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the current year?
questions.explanation:
Passive activity losses generally offset only passive income (IRC §469). However, when a taxpayer disposes of the entire interest in a passive activity in a fully taxable transaction, the current-year loss and all suspended losses from that activity are treated as not from a passive activity and may be deducted against nonpassive income (IRC §469(g)).

Salary = $50,000
Income from partnership A (material participation, nonpassive) = $20,000
Current-year loss from partnership B = ($40,000)
Suspended loss from partnership B freed on disposition = ($10,000)
AGI = $50,000 + $20,000 - $40,000 - $10,000 = $20,000

The $30,000 amount deducts the current-year loss but not the $10,000 suspended loss.
The $60,000 amount deducts only the suspended loss.
The $70,000 amount disallows all losses from partnership B, ignoring the release of losses on disposition.
questions.explanationJa:
パッシブ損失は原則としてパッシブ所得とのみ相殺できるが、パッシブ活動の持分全部を課税取引で処分した年は、その活動の当期損失と繰越停止損失の全額を非パッシブ所得から控除できる（IRC §469(g)）。
給与 $50,000 + A（実質的関与・非パッシブ）$20,000 − B 当期損失 $40,000 − 繰越停止損失 $10,000 = AGI $20,000。
$30,000 は繰越停止損失を控除していない。$60,000 は繰越停止損失だけを控除している。$70,000 は B の損失を全く控除していない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2011 Recently Released Q.33 (AICPA No. 9973)

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer reports the following items for the current year. Partnership A operates a movie theater in which the taxpayer materially participates. Partnership B operates an equipment rental business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate. The building is rented to a third party.

Ordinary income from partnership A | $70,000
Net loss from partnership B | (9,000)
Rental income from building | 7,000
Short-term capital gain from sale of stock | 4,000

What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469, income and losses from passive activities are netted, and a net passive loss is not deductible against nonpassive income. Rental activities are passive by definition (§469(c)(2)), and a trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate is passive (§469(c)(1)). The $25,000 rental real estate allowance (§469(i)) does not apply because the loss comes from an equipment rental business, not rental real estate.

Nonpassive income: movie theater (material participation) = $70,000
Portfolio income: short-term capital gain = $4,000
Passive items: equipment rental loss ($9,000) + building rental income $7,000 = ($2,000) net passive loss, suspended
AGI = $70,000 + $4,000 = $74,000

The $70,000 amount omits the short-term capital gain.
The $72,000 amount deducts the $2,000 net passive loss against nonpassive income.
The $77,000 amount treats the $7,000 of rental income as nonpassive income without netting it against the passive loss.
questions.explanationJa:
パッシブ活動の所得と損失は互いに通算し、通算後のパッシブ損失は非パッシブ所得から控除できない（IRC §469）。賃貸活動は定義上パッシブ（§469(c)(2)）、実質的関与の無い事業もパッシブ（§469(c)(1)）。損失は機器賃貸事業から生じているので、不動産賃貸の $25,000 特例（§469(i)）は使えない。
非パッシブ: 映画館 $70,000、ポートフォリオ: 短期譲渡益 $4,000、パッシブ: 機器賃貸 −$9,000 + 建物賃貸 $7,000 = −$2,000（繰越）。AGI = $70,000 + $4,000 = $74,000。
$70,000 は短期譲渡益を漏らしている。$72,000 は通算後のパッシブ損失 $2,000 を控除している。$77,000 は賃貸収入を非パッシブとして扱っている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.11 (AICPA No. 89811)

questions.stem: On February 1, year 1, a taxpayer purchased an option to buy 1,000 shares of XYZ Co. for $200 per share. The taxpayer purchased the option for $50,000, which was to remain in effect for six months. The market declined, and the taxpayer let the option lapse on August 1, year 1. The taxpayer would report which of the following as a capital loss on the year 1 income tax return?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $50,000 long term

choices.label: B
choices.text: $50,000 short term

choices.label: C
choices.text: $150,000 long term

choices.label: D
choices.text: $200,000 short term

questions.explanation:
When an option to buy property expires unexercised, the holder is treated as having sold the option on the date it lapses, and the loss has the same character the underlying stock would have (IRC §1234(a)). Stock is a capital asset, so the loss is a capital loss equal to the $50,000 paid for the option. The holding period runs from February 1 to August 1, year 1, which is not more than one year, so the loss is short term.

The $50,000 long-term amount is incorrect because the option was held only six months.
The $150,000 and $200,000 amounts are based on the value of the underlying shares rather than the taxpayer's investment. The taxpayer never acquired the shares, so the loss is limited to the $50,000 cost of the option.
questions.explanationJa:
購入したオプションを行使せずに失効させた場合、失効日に売却したものとみなされ、損失の性格は原資産（株式）と同じになる（IRC §1234(a)）。株式は資本資産なので、支払ったオプション料 $50,000 がキャピタルロスとなる。保有期間は2月1日〜8月1日の6か月で1年以下なので短期。
$50,000 の長期は保有期間が6か月なので誤り。$150,000 や $200,000 は投資額と関係が無く、株式は取得していないので損失はオプション料に限られる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 89813)

questions.stem: A taxpayer lived in an apartment building and had a two-year lease that began 16 months ago. The taxpayer's landlord wanted to sell the building and offered the taxpayer $10,000 to vacate the apartment immediately. The taxpayer's lease on the apartment was a capital asset but had no tax basis. If the taxpayer accepted the landlord's offer, the gain or loss would be which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An ordinary gain

choices.label: B
choices.text: A short-term capital loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: A long-term capital gain

choices.label: D
choices.text: A short-term capital gain

questions.explanation:
Amounts received by a lessee for the cancellation of a lease are treated as amounts received in exchange for the lease (IRC §1241). Because the lease is a capital asset in the taxpayer's hands, the payment produces capital gain. The taxpayer has no basis, so the entire $10,000 is gain. The lease was held for 16 months, which is more than one year, so the gain is long term.

An ordinary gain is incorrect because §1241 treats the cancellation payment as a sale or exchange of the capital asset.
A short-term capital loss is incorrect because the taxpayer receives $10,000 with no basis, which is a gain.
A short-term capital gain is incorrect because the holding period exceeds one year.
questions.explanationJa:
賃借人が賃貸借契約の解約の対価として受け取る金額は、賃借権の譲渡の対価とみなされる（IRC §1241）。本問の賃借権は資本資産なのでキャピタルゲインとなり、basis が無いので $10,000 全額が利益。保有期間は16か月で1年超なので長期。
通常所得ではない（§1241 で譲渡として扱う）。basis ゼロで $10,000 を受け取るので損失ではない。保有期間が1年を超えるので短期ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.14 (AICPA No. 89814)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the deductibility of an individual's medical expenses?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A medical expense paid by credit card is deductible in the year the credit card bill is paid.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A medical expense deduction is allowed for payments made in the current year for medical services received in earlier years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Medical expenses, net of insurance reimbursements, are disregarded in the alternative minimum tax calculation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A medical expense deduction is not allowed for Medicare insurance premiums.

questions.explanation:
Medical expenses are deductible in the year paid, regardless of when the services were provided (Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(a)(1)). A payment made this year for medical services received in an earlier year is deductible this year, provided the expenses were not deducted before.

A medical expense charged on a credit card is treated as paid when charged, not when the credit card bill is paid.
Medical expenses are not disregarded for the alternative minimum tax; they are allowed in computing AMTI to the extent they exceed the AGI floor.
Medicare insurance premiums (for example, Medicare Part B premiums) are deductible as medical insurance.
questions.explanationJa:
医療費は、サービスを受けた時期にかかわらず、支払った年に控除する（Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(a)(1)）。過年度に受けた治療の費用を当年に支払えば、（過去に控除していなければ）当年に控除できる。
クレジットカード払いは、カード請求の支払時ではなく、カードで決済した時に支払ったものとされる。AMT の計算でも医療費は AGI 基準額を超える部分が控除でき、無視されるわけではない。Medicare の保険料（Part B など）も医療保険料として控除対象となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.18 (AICPA No. 89818)

questions.stem: Upon her grandfather's death, Jordan inherited 10 shares of Universal Corp. stock that had a fair market value of $5,000. Her grandfather acquired the shares in 1995 for $2,500. Four months after her grandfather's death, Jordan sold all her shares of Universal for $7,500. What was Jordan's recognized gain in the year of sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $2,500 long-term capital gain

choices.label: B
choices.text: $2,500 short-term capital gain

choices.label: C
choices.text: $5,000 long-term capital gain

choices.label: D
choices.text: $5,000 short-term capital gain

questions.explanation:
The basis of property acquired from a decedent is generally its fair market value at the date of death (IRC §1014(a)). Property acquired from a decedent is treated as held for more than one year, regardless of how long the heir actually holds it (IRC §1223(9)), so the gain is long term.

Basis = $5,000 fair market value at death
Gain = $7,500 - $5,000 = $2,500 long-term capital gain

A short-term characterization is incorrect because inherited property automatically receives a long-term holding period even though Jordan held the shares only four months.
The $5,000 gain amounts use the grandfather's $2,500 cost as basis; carryover basis does not apply to inherited property.
questions.explanationJa:
相続により取得した資産の basis は、原則として死亡日の時価となる（IRC §1014(a)）。また相続資産は実際の保有期間にかかわらず1年超保有したものとみなされる（§1223(9)）。
basis = $5,000、利益 = $7,500 − $5,000 = $2,500 の長期キャピタルゲイン。
短期とするのは誤りで、保有4か月でも相続資産は長期扱い。$5,000 の利益は祖父の取得価額 $2,500 を引き継いでおり、相続資産には適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.23 (AICPA No. 89823)

questions.stem: In the current year, Fitz, a single taxpayer, sustained a $48,000 loss on Code Sec. 1244 stock in JJJ Corp., a qualifying small business corporation, and a $20,000 loss on Code Sec. 1244 stock in MMM Corp., another qualifying small business corporation. What is the maximum amount of loss that Fitz can deduct for the current year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $50,000 capital loss

choices.label: B
choices.text: $68,000 capital loss

choices.label: C
choices.text: $18,000 ordinary loss and $50,000 capital loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: $50,000 ordinary loss and $18,000 capital loss

questions.explanation:
A loss on Section 1244 stock is an ordinary loss, limited in any one year to $50,000 for a single taxpayer ($100,000 on a joint return) (IRC §1244(a), (b)). The limit applies to the aggregate of all §1244 losses for the year, not per corporation. Loss in excess of the limit is a capital loss.

Total §1244 losses = $48,000 + $20,000 = $68,000
Ordinary loss (limit for single taxpayer) = $50,000
Capital loss = $68,000 - $50,000 = $18,000

Treating the losses entirely as capital losses ($50,000 or $68,000 capital loss) ignores the ordinary loss treatment of §1244.
$18,000 ordinary and $50,000 capital reverses the allocation; the first $50,000 is ordinary.
questions.explanationJa:
§1244 株式の損失は通常損失となり、年間の上限は単身者 $50,000（夫婦合算 $100,000）。上限は会社ごとではなく、その年の §1244 損失の合計に適用され、超過分はキャピタルロスとなる（IRC §1244(a)、(b)）。
損失合計 = $48,000 + $20,000 = $68,000、通常損失 $50,000、キャピタルロス $18,000。
全額をキャピタルロスとするものは §1244 の通常損失扱いを無視している。通常損失 $18,000・キャピタルロス $50,000 は配分が逆。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2012 Recently Released Q.25 (AICPA No. 89825)

questions.stem: Johnson worked for ABC Co. and earned a salary of $100,000. Johnson also received, as a fringe benefit, group term-life insurance at twice Johnson's salary. The annual IRS-established uniform cost of insurance is $2.76 per $1,000. What amount must Johnson include in gross income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §79, the cost of employer-provided group-term life insurance coverage up to $50,000 is excluded from the employee's gross income. The cost of coverage above $50,000, measured using the IRS uniform premium rates, is included.

Coverage = 2 x $100,000 = $200,000
Excess coverage = $200,000 - $50,000 = $150,000
Included cost = $150,000 / $1,000 x $2.76 = $414
Gross income = $100,000 salary + $414 = $100,414

The $100,000 amount excludes all of the insurance benefit, but only the first $50,000 of coverage is tax-free. The $100,276 amount applies the rate to only $100,000 of coverage. The $100,552 amount applies the rate to the full $200,000 of coverage without the $50,000 exclusion.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §79により、雇用主負担の団体定期生命保険は保険金額$50,000までの保険料相当額が非課税で、超過部分の保険料相当額（IRSの統一料率で計算）が総所得に算入される。

保険金額 = $100,000 × 2 = $200,000
超過保険金額 = $200,000 − $50,000 = $150,000
算入額 = $150,000 ÷ $1,000 × $2.76 = $414
総所得 = 給与$100,000 + $414 = $100,414

$100,000は保険の便益を全額非課税としており誤り。$100,276は$100,000分の保険にしか料率を適用していない。$100,552は$50,000の非課税枠を控除せず$200,000全額に料率を適用している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.6 (AICPA No. 90206)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements regarding an individual's suspended passive activity losses is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $3,000 of suspended losses can be utilized each year against portfolio income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Suspended losses can be carried forward, but not back, until utilized.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Suspended losses must be carried back three years and forward seven years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A maximum of 50% of the suspended losses can be used each year when an election is made to forgo the carry-back period.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(b), passive activity losses that are disallowed in the current year are suspended and carried forward indefinitely to offset passive income in future years. There is no carryback. Any remaining suspended losses are fully deductible when the taxpayer disposes of the entire interest in the activity in a fully taxable transaction to an unrelated party (IRC §469(g)).

The $3,000 annual limit applies to net capital losses against ordinary income, not to passive losses, and passive losses cannot offset portfolio income. There is no three-year carryback and seven-year carryforward for passive losses. There is no election to forgo a carryback that allows 50% of suspended losses to be used each year.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(b)により、当期に控除できなかったパッシブ損失は停止され、将来のパッシブ所得と相殺するために無期限に繰り越される。繰戻しはない。活動の持分全体を非関連者に課税取引で処分したときに、残る停止損失は全額控除できる（§469(g)）。

年$3,000の上限は純資本損失を通常所得と相殺する際のもので、パッシブ損失には関係なく、パッシブ損失はポートフォリオ所得と相殺できない。3年繰戻し・7年繰越しという規定はない。繰戻しを放棄すれば毎年50%使えるという選択制度もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.17 (AICPA No. 90217)

questions.stem: Smith has an adjusted gross income (AGI) of $120,000 without taking into consideration $40,000 of losses from rental real estate activities. Smith actively participates in the rental real estate activities. What amount of the rental losses may Smith deduct in determining taxable income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), an individual who actively participates in a rental real estate activity may deduct up to $25,000 of rental losses against nonpassive income. The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of the amount by which modified AGI exceeds $100,000 (fully phased out at $150,000).

Excess of AGI over $100,000 = $120,000 - $100,000 = $20,000
Reduction = 50% x $20,000 = $10,000
Allowance = $25,000 - $10,000 = $15,000
Deductible rental loss = lesser of $40,000 loss or $15,000 allowance = $15,000

The $0 amount ignores the active participation allowance. The $20,000 amount is the excess of AGI over $100,000, not the remaining allowance. The $40,000 amount allows the full loss, which exceeds the maximum allowance.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産活動に積極的に関与する個人は、賃貸損失を最大$25,000まで非パッシブ所得と相殺できる。この枠は修正AGIが$100,000を超える額の50%だけ減額される（$150,000で消滅）。

AGIの超過額 = $120,000 − $100,000 = $20,000
減額 = 50% × $20,000 = $10,000
控除枠 = $25,000 − $10,000 = $15,000
控除できる賃貸損失 = 損失$40,000と枠$15,000の小さい方 = $15,000

$0は積極的関与の特例を無視している。$20,000はAGIの超過額で、残る控除枠ではない。$40,000は上限を超えて全額を控除している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2013 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. 90230)

questions.stem:
Individual Lark's year 2 brokerage account statement listed the following capital gains and losses from the sale of stock investments:

Short-term capital gain | $ 6,000
Long-term capital gain | 14,000
Short-term capital loss | 4,000
Long-term capital loss | 8,000

In addition, two stock investments became worthless in year 2. Public Company X stock was purchased in December, year 1, for $5,000, and formal notification was received by Lark on July, year 2, that it was worthless. Private company Section 1244 stock was issued to Lark for $10,000 in January, year 1, and was determined to be worthless in December, year 2. What is Lark's year 2 net capital gain or loss before any capital loss limitation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $2,000 net capital loss

choices.label: B
choices.text: $3,000 net capital gain

choices.label: C
choices.text: $7,000 net capital loss

choices.label: D
choices.text: $8,000 net capital gain

questions.explanation:
Worthless securities that are capital assets are treated under IRC §165(g)(1) as sold on the last day of the taxable year in which they become worthless. Losses on Section 1244 stock are ordinary losses (up to $50,000, or $100,000 on a joint return) under IRC §1244(a), so they are not part of the capital gain and loss netting.

Net short-term: $6,000 gain - $4,000 loss = $2,000 net short-term gain
Net long-term before worthless stock: $14,000 gain - $8,000 loss = $6,000
Company X stock (bought December, year 1; deemed sold December 31, year 2; held more than one year): $5,000 long-term capital loss
Net long-term: $6,000 - $5,000 = $1,000 net long-term gain
Section 1244 stock $10,000 loss: ordinary loss, excluded from capital netting
Net capital gain = $2,000 + $1,000 = $3,000

The $2,000 net capital loss ($2,000 + $6,000 - $10,000) treats the Section 1244 loss as a capital loss and omits the Company X loss. The $7,000 net capital loss ($3,000 - $10,000) treats the $10,000 Section 1244 loss as a capital loss. The $8,000 net capital gain ($2,000 + $6,000) ignores the $5,000 Company X worthless stock loss.
questions.explanationJa:
資本資産である有価証券が無価値となった場合、IRC §165(g)(1)により無価値となった年の最終日に売却したものとみなす。Section 1244株式の損失は§1244(a)により通常損失（単独$50,000・夫婦合算$100,000まで）となり、資本損益の通算には含めない。

短期: 利得$6,000 − 損失$4,000 = 純短期利得$2,000
長期（無価値株式前）: 利得$14,000 − 損失$8,000 = $6,000
X社株（year 1年12月取得、year 2年12月31日に売却とみなす、保有1年超）: 長期資本損失$5,000
純長期利得 = $6,000 − $5,000 = $1,000
Section 1244株式の損失$10,000: 通常損失で資本損益の通算から除外
純資本利得 = $2,000 + $1,000 = $3,000

$2,000の純損失（$2,000＋$6,000−$10,000）はSection 1244株式の損失を資本損失とし、X社株の損失を落としている。$7,000の純損失（$3,000−$10,000）は$10,000のSection 1244株式損失を資本損失として扱っている。$8,000の純利得（$2,000＋$6,000）はX社株の$5,000の損失を無視している。

questions.stem:
A review of Bearing's year 2 records disclosed the following tax information:

Wages | $18,000
Taxable interest and qualifying dividends | 4,000
Schedule C trucking business net income | 32,000
Rental (loss) from residential property | (35,000)
Limited partnership (loss) | (5,000)

Bearing actively participated in the rental property and was a limited partner in the partnership. Bearing had sufficient amounts at risk for the rental property and the partnership. What is Bearing's year 2 adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
Passive losses can generally offset only passive income (IRC §469(a)). A limited partner's interest is treated as passive (IRC §469(h)(2)), and Bearing has no passive income, so the $5,000 limited partnership loss is suspended. Under the IRC §469(i) exception, up to $25,000 of losses from rental real estate in which the taxpayer actively participates can offset nonpassive income; the allowance is not reduced because modified AGI (computed without the passive losses) of $54,000 is below $100,000.

Wages: $18,000
Interest and dividends: + $4,000
Schedule C net income: + $32,000
Income before passive losses = $54,000
Rental loss allowed (limited to $25,000 of the $35,000 loss): - $25,000
Limited partnership loss (suspended): $0
AGI = $29,000

The $14,000 amount deducts the full $35,000 rental loss and the $5,000 partnership loss. The $19,000 amount deducts the full $35,000 rental loss. The $54,000 amount allows none of the rental loss despite active participation.
questions.explanationJa:
パッシブ損失は原則としてパッシブ所得とのみ相殺できる（§469(a)）。リミテッド・パートナーの持分はパッシブとされ（§469(h)(2)）、Bearingにはパッシブ所得がないので、LPの損失$5,000は停止される。§469(i)の特例により、積極的に関与する賃貸不動産の損失は$25,000まで非パッシブ所得と相殺でき、修正AGI（パッシブ損失考慮前）$54,000は$100,000未満なので枠は減額されない。

給与 $18,000
利子・配当 ＋$4,000
Schedule C純利益 ＋$32,000
パッシブ損失前の所得 = $54,000
賃貸損失（$35,000のうち$25,000まで）−$25,000
LP損失（停止）$0
AGI = $29,000

$14,000は賃貸損失$35,000とLP損失$5,000を全額控除している。$19,000は賃貸損失$35,000を全額控除している。$54,000は積極的関与があるのに賃貸損失を一切認めていない。

questions.stem: Baker, an unmarried individual, sold a personal residence, which has an adjusted basis of $70,000, for $165,000. Baker owned and lived in the residence for seven years. Selling expenses were $10,000. Four weeks prior to the sale, Baker paid a handyman $1,000 to paint and fix-up the residence. What is the amount of Baker's recognized gain?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §121, an unmarried taxpayer who owned and used a home as a principal residence for at least 2 of the 5 years before the sale may exclude up to $250,000 of gain. Baker owned and lived in the home for seven years, so the exclusion applies. Selling expenses reduce the amount realized; fix-up (painting and repair) costs are not deductible or added to basis, but they do not change the result here.

Amount realized = $165,000 - $10,000 selling expenses = $155,000
Realized gain = $155,000 - $70,000 basis = $85,000
Excluded gain (up to $250,000) = $85,000
Recognized gain = $0

The $84,000 amount subtracts the $1,000 fix-up cost and also ignores the exclusion. The $85,000 amount is the realized gain before the §121 exclusion. The $95,000 amount ignores both the selling expenses and the exclusion.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §121により、売却前5年のうち2年以上所有し主たる住居として使用した住宅を売却した未婚者は、$250,000まで利得を非課税にできる。Bakerは7年間所有・居住しているので適用される。売却費用は譲渡対価から控除する。塗装・修繕費（fix-up費用）は控除もベーシス加算もできないが、本問の結論には影響しない。

譲渡対価 = $165,000 − 売却費用$10,000 = $155,000
実現利得 = $155,000 − ベーシス$70,000 = $85,000
非課税額（$250,000まで）= $85,000
認識利得 = $0

$84,000はfix-up費用$1,000を差し引いたうえ非課税措置を無視している。$85,000は§121適用前の実現利得。$95,000は売却費用と非課税措置の両方を無視している。

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the deductibility of donations made to qualifying charities by a cash-basis individual taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A contemporaneous written acknowledgement is required for donations of $100.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A charitable contribution deduction is not allowed for the value of services rendered to a charity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A qualified appraisal for real property donations is not required to be attached to the tax return unless the property value exceeds $10,000.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The charitable contribution deduction for long-term appreciated stock is limited to 50% of adjusted gross income.

questions.explanation:
Under Treas. Reg. §1.170A-1(g), no charitable deduction is allowed for the value of a taxpayer's time or services contributed to a charity; only unreimbursed out-of-pocket expenses incurred in rendering the services may be deducted.

A contemporaneous written acknowledgment is required for a single contribution of $250 or more (IRC §170(f)(8)), not $100. A qualified appraisal is required for noncash property (other than certain publicly traded securities) valued over $5,000, and the appraisal must be attached to the return only when the claimed value exceeds $500,000, so a $10,000 threshold is incorrect. The deduction for long-term capital gain property such as appreciated stock contributed to a public charity is generally limited to 30% of AGI (IRC §170(b)(1)), not 50%.
questions.explanationJa:
Treas. Reg. §1.170A-1(g)により、慈善団体に提供した時間や役務の価値は寄附金控除の対象にならない。控除できるのは役務提供に伴って自己負担した実費（未償還分）だけである。

同時期の書面による受領確認が必要なのは1回$250以上の寄附で、$100ではない（§170(f)(8)）。適格鑑定は$5,000超の非現金資産（一部の上場有価証券を除く）に必要で、鑑定書の添付が求められるのは評価額が$500,000を超える場合なので、$10,000という基準は誤り。値上がりした長期保有株式など長期キャピタルゲイン資産の公益慈善団体への寄附は原則AGIの30%が上限で、50%ではない（§170(b)(1)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 90563)

questions.stem: Nan, a cash basis taxpayer, borrowed money from a bank and signed a 10 year interest-bearing note on business property on January 1 of the current year. The cash flow from Nan's business enabled Nan to prepay the first three years of interest attributable to the note on December 31 of the current year. How should Nan treat the prepayment of interest for tax purposes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deduct the entire amount as a current expense

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deduct the current year’s interest and amortize the balance over the next two years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capitalize the interest and amortize the balance over the 10-year loan period

choices.label: D
choices.text: Capitalize the interest as part of the basis of the business property

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §461(g)(1), a cash-basis taxpayer who prepays interest must treat the prepaid interest as paid in the period to which it is allocable, as if the taxpayer used the accrual method. Nan may deduct only the interest attributable to the current year; the interest prepaid for the next two years is deducted in those years.

Deducting the entire three years of interest currently is not permitted because §461(g) overrides the normal cash-method rule for prepaid interest. Amortizing over the 10-year loan period spreads the interest over years to which it does not relate; the prepayment covers only three years. Interest on a loan is not added to the basis of business property merely because the loan is secured by that property.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §461(g)(1)により、現金主義の納税者が前払いした利息は、発生主義と同様に、その利息が帰属する期間に支払ったものとして扱われる。Nanが当年に控除できるのは当年分の利息だけで、翌年以降2年分の前払利息はそれぞれの年に控除する。

3年分を一括で当年控除することは、§461(g)が前払利息について現金主義の通常ルールに優先するため認められない。10年のローン期間で償却するのは、前払いが3年分にすぎないのに関係のない年に配分しており誤り。事業用資産を担保とする借入れの利息だからといって、その資産のベーシスに加算されるわけではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.27 (AICPA No. 90577)

questions.stem: The Jacksons, who file a joint return, actively participate in a solely-owned rental real estate activity that produces a $30,000 loss during the current year. Their adjusted gross income was $120,000 before considering the rental activity. How much of the rental loss, if any, are the Jacksons entitled to deduct?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), an individual who actively participates in a rental real estate activity may deduct up to $25,000 of rental losses against nonpassive income. The $25,000 allowance is reduced by 50% of modified AGI over $100,000 (fully phased out at $150,000).

Allowance before phase-out: $25,000
Reduction: ($120,000 − $100,000) × 50% = $10,000
Allowable loss: $25,000 − $10,000 = $15,000

The remaining $15,000 of the $30,000 loss is suspended and carried forward as a passive loss.

The $0 amount ignores the active-participation exception. The $25,000 amount ignores the AGI phase-out. The $30,000 amount allows the entire loss, but the special allowance is capped at $25,000 before the phase-out.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産に積極的に関与（active participation）する個人は、賃貸損失を最大$25,000まで他の所得と通算できる。この枠は修正AGIが$100,000を超える部分の50%だけ縮小する（$150,000で消滅）。

縮小前の枠: $25,000
縮小額: ($120,000 − $100,000) × 50% = $10,000
控除可能額: $25,000 − $10,000 = $15,000

$30,000の損失のうち残り$15,000はパッシブ損失として繰り越される。

$0は積極的関与の特例を無視している。$25,000はAGIによる縮小を無視している。$30,000は損失全額を認めているが、特例枠は縮小前でも$25,000が上限である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2014 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 90582)

questions.stem:
As a result of a divorce, a taxpayer received the following during the current year:

Cash from the property settlement | $100,000
Child support | 12,000
Alimony payments | 30,000

What amount, if any, must be included in gross income for the current year?
questions.explanation:
The question treats the amounts as received in the current year as a result of a divorce, so the divorce instrument is treated as executed after December 31, 2018. For such instruments, the TCJA repealed the inclusion of alimony in the recipient's gross income (former IRC §71) and the payer's deduction (former §215). Alimony received is therefore excluded.

Cash from the property settlement: excluded (transfer between spouses incident to divorce, IRC §1041) → $0
Child support: never included in the recipient's income → $0
Alimony payments: excluded for post-2018 divorce instruments → $0
Total gross income: $0

The $30,000 amount applies the pre-2019 rule that included alimony in income. The $130,000 amount also includes the property settlement, and the $142,000 amount includes all three items, including child support.
questions.explanationJa:
問題は当年に離婚に伴って受け取った金額を扱っているので、離婚証書は2018年12月31日より後に作成されたものとして扱う。TCJAにより、2019年以降の離婚証書に基づく扶養料（alimony）は受取側の総所得に含まれず（旧IRC §71）、支払側も控除できない（旧§215）。

財産分与の現金: 離婚に伴う配偶者間の移転として非課税（IRC §1041）→ $0
子の養育費: 受取側の所得にならない → $0
扶養料: 2019年以降の離婚証書では非課税 → $0
総所得算入額: $0

$30,000は扶養料を所得に含めていた2018年以前の規定を当てはめている。$130,000はさらに財産分与を含め、$142,000は養育費まで含めている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 90812)

questions.stem: Thompson's spouse died in year 1. Thompson did not remarry in year 2 and lived alone the entire year. What is Thompson's year 2 filing status?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Married filing jointly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Surviving spouse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Head of household

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer whose spouse died in year 1 may file a joint return for year 1 (the year of death). In year 2, a joint return is no longer available because Thompson is not married. Surviving spouse (qualifying widow(er)) status for the two years after the year of death requires maintaining a household for a dependent child (IRC §2(a)), and head of household status requires maintaining a household for a qualifying person (IRC §2(b)). Thompson lived alone the entire year 2, so neither applies, and Thompson files as single.

Married filing jointly applies only for the year of the spouse's death. Surviving spouse and head of household both require a qualifying child or other qualifying person living in the home, which Thompson does not have.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者が1年目に死亡した場合、死亡年である1年目は夫婦合算申告ができる。2年目は婚姻状態ではないため合算申告はできない。死亡年の翌2年間に使える適格寡婦（夫）（surviving spouse）は扶養する子と同居する世帯の維持が条件（IRC §2(a)）で、世帯主（head of household）も適格者のための世帯の維持が条件（IRC §2(b)）である。Thompsonは2年目に一人暮らしなので、どちらにも当たらず独身（single）となる。

夫婦合算申告は配偶者の死亡年に限られる。適格寡婦（夫）と世帯主は、いずれも同居する扶養の子や適格者が必要で、Thompsonには該当者がいない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.13 (AICPA No. 90813)

questions.stem: Logan, an employee of Argon Industries, earned a salary of $60,000 in year 2. In addition, the following two transactions between Logan and Argon occurred in year 2: Logan received a bonus of 100 shares of publicly-traded stock worth $13,000 with a basis to Argon of $8,000, and Logan purchased 1,000 shares of unrestricted Argon stock pursuant to a nonqualifying stock option plan for $10 per share when stock was valued at $25 per share. What amount of compensation should Argon report in Logan's Form W-2 for year 2?
questions.explanation:
Compensation reported on Form W-2 includes cash wages and the fair market value of property transferred to the employee for services. When an employee exercises a nonqualified stock option that has no readily ascertainable fair market value at grant, the spread at exercise (fair market value less the exercise price) is compensation (Treas. Reg. §1.83-7).

Salary: $60,000
Stock bonus at fair market value: $13,000
Nonqualified option spread: 1,000 shares × ($25 − $10) = $15,000
Total W-2 compensation: $60,000 + $13,000 + $15,000 = $88,000

Argon's $8,000 basis in the bonus shares affects Argon's own gain on transferring the shares, not the amount of Logan's compensation. The $60,000 amount omits both stock items. The $73,000 amount omits the option spread. The $93,000 amount overstates the stock-related income; only the $13,000 fair market value of the bonus shares and the $15,000 option spread are compensation.
questions.explanationJa:
W-2に記載する報酬には、現金給与に加え、役務の対価として従業員に移転した資産の時価が含まれる。付与時に時価が容易に算定できない非適格ストックオプションを行使した場合、行使時の時価と行使価格の差額が報酬になる（Treas. Reg. §1.83-7）。

給与: $60,000
賞与として受けた株式の時価: $13,000
非適格オプションの差額: 1,000株 × ($25 − $10) = $15,000
W-2報酬合計: $60,000 + $13,000 + $15,000 = $88,000

賞与株式のArgon側の取得価額$8,000は、Argonが株式を移転したときの利得に関係するだけで、Loganの報酬額には影響しない。$60,000は株式関連の2項目を落としている。$73,000はオプションの差額を落としている。$93,000は株式関連の所得を過大にしており、報酬になるのは賞与株式の時価$13,000とオプションの差額$15,000だけである。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.33 (AICPA No. 90833)

questions.stem: Flowers, a married taxpayer, purchased an annuity for $64,400 that will pay $700 per month over the life of Flowers and Flowers' spouse. At the time of purchase the couple's joint life expectancy was 23 years. Flowers received payment beginning April 1, year 1 amounting to $6,300 in the first year of the annuity contract. How much is includible in Flowers' gross income in the first year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §72(b), each annuity payment is excluded from gross income in the ratio of the investment in the contract to the expected return under the contract.

Expected return: $700 × 12 months × 23 years = $193,200
Exclusion ratio: $64,400 ÷ $193,200 = 1/3
Payments received in year 1: $6,300 (9 payments of $700)
Excluded portion: $6,300 × 1/3 = $2,100
Includible in gross income: $6,300 − $2,100 = $4,200

The $0 amount treats all payments as a return of investment. The $2,100 amount is the excluded portion, not the taxable portion. The $6,300 amount ignores the recovery of the $64,400 investment.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §72(b)により、年金の各受取額のうち、投資額（払込額）÷期待受取総額の割合だけが総所得から除外される。

期待受取総額: $700 × 12か月 × 23年 = $193,200
除外割合: $64,400 ÷ $193,200 = 1/3
1年目の受取額: $6,300（$700 × 9回）
除外額: $6,300 × 1/3 = $2,100
総所得算入額: $6,300 − $2,100 = $4,200

$0は受取額全額を投資の回収としている。$2,100は除外額であり課税部分ではない。$6,300は投資額$64,400の回収を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2015 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. 90834)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the alternative minimum tax (AMT) of an individual is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is determined from the tax rate schedules and computed on income that exceeds $100,000.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is computed on an individual's regular taxable income at a rate of 28%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is calculated after certain tax preference items that may be used as an alternative to the regular tax are deducted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: AMT credits may be carried forward to future tax years.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §53, the minimum tax credit for AMT paid that is attributable to deferral items (timing differences) is carried forward indefinitely and may offset regular tax in future years to the extent regular tax exceeds tentative minimum tax. AMT credits may therefore be carried forward.

The AMT is not computed by applying the regular tax rate schedules to income over $100,000; it is computed by applying the AMT rates of 26% and 28% (§55(b)) to alternative minimum taxable income after the AMT exemption. It is not computed on regular taxable income at a flat 28% rate, because regular taxable income must first be increased by adjustments and preferences to arrive at AMTI. Tax preference items are added back to taxable income, not deducted.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §53により、繰延項目（タイミング差異）に起因して納付したAMTは最低税額控除（minimum tax credit）として無期限に繰り越し、将来の年度に通常の税額が仮最低税額を超える範囲で通常の税額から控除できる。したがってAMTクレジットは繰越可能である。

AMTは$100,000超の所得に通常の税率表を当てはめて計算するものではなく、AMT控除後の代替最低課税所得（AMTI）に26%・28%のAMT税率（§55(b)）を適用して計算する。通常の課税所得にそのまま28%を掛けるのでもなく、まず調整項目・優遇項目を加減してAMTIを求める。優遇項目は課税所得に加算するもので、控除するものではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2016 Recently Released Q.31 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem:
Jensen reported the following items during the current year:

Fair rent value of employer-owned condominium | $ 1,400
Cash found in a $30 flea-market desk | 400
Inheritance | 11,000

The employer allowed Jensen to use the condominium for free in recognition of outstanding achievement.
Based on this information, what is Jensen's gross income for the year?
questions.explanation:
Gross income includes all income from whatever source derived (IRC §61). The free use of the employer's condominium is compensation for services, and its fair rental value ($1,400) is taxable; it is not an excludable employee achievement award, which must be tangible personal property under §274(j). Cash found in the desk is treasure trove and is income when reduced to undisputed possession (Treas. Reg. §1.61-14(a)), so the full $400 is included. An inheritance is excluded under §102(a).

Gross income = $1,400 + $400 = $1,800

The $1,400 amount omits the found cash. The $1,770 amount reduces the found cash by the $30 desk price, but the $30 is the cost of the desk, not an offset against the cash found. The $12,400 amount includes the excludable $11,000 inheritance and omits the found cash.
questions.explanationJa:
総所得にはあらゆる源泉からの所得が含まれる（IRC §61）。雇用主のコンドミニアムの無償使用は役務の対価であり、公正賃料$1,400は課税される。従業員功労賞の除外は有形動産に限られる（§274(j)）ため該当しない。机から見つけた現金は埋蔵物（treasure trove）として、争いなく占有した時点で所得となる（Treas. Reg. §1.61-14(a)）ので$400全額を含める。相続は§102(a)で除外される。

総所得 = $1,400 + $400 = $1,800

$1,400は見つけた現金を漏らしている。$1,770は現金から机の代金$30を差し引いているが、$30は机の取得費であり現金の所得を減らさない。$12,400は除外される相続$11,000を含め、見つけた現金を漏らしている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.10 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem:
Dr. Merry, a self-employed dentist, incurred the following expenses:

Investment expenses | $700
Custodial fees for Dr. Merry's Keogh plan | 40
Work uniforms for Dr. Merry and employees | 320
Periodicals for the waiting room | 110
Dental education seminar | 1,300

What is the amount of expenses the doctor can deduct as business expenses on Schedule C, Profit or Loss from Business?
questions.explanation:
Schedule C deductions are ordinary and necessary expenses of the taxpayer's trade or business (IRC §162). Work uniforms not suitable for ordinary wear ($320), periodicals for patients in the reception area ($110), and a dental education seminar that maintains or improves the dentist's skills ($1,300) are business expenses.

Schedule C deductions = $320 + $110 + $1,300 = $1,730

Investment expenses ($700) relate to producing investment income under §212, not to the dental practice, and are not Schedule C expenses. Custodial fees for the dentist's own Keogh plan ($40) relate to the owner's personal retirement account, not to operating the business. The $1,770 amount adds the Keogh fees, and the $2,430 amount adds the investment expenses. The $1,620 amount omits the $110 of reception-area periodicals.
questions.explanationJa:
Schedule Cで控除できるのは、事業に通常かつ必要な経費である（IRC §162）。普段着に適さない仕事用の制服$320、待合室用の定期刊行物$110、歯科医としての技能を維持・向上させる研修$1,300は事業経費である。

Schedule Cの控除額 = $320 + $110 + $1,300 = $1,730

投資費用$700は§212の投資所得に関するもので、歯科業務の経費ではない。本人のKeoghプランの管理手数料$40は本人の退職口座に関するもので、事業運営の経費ではない。$1,770はKeogh手数料を、$2,430は投資費用を加えた額で、$1,620は待合室の定期刊行物$110を漏らした額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.11 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: The term active participation for a passive activity loss is relevant in relation to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rental real estate activities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Working interests in oil and gas properties.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Passive activities in which the taxpayer materially participates.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Passive activities in which the taxpayer does not materially participate.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), an individual who actively participates in a rental real estate activity may deduct up to $25,000 of passive losses from that activity against nonpassive income, phased out as modified AGI rises from $100,000 to $150,000. Active participation is a lower standard than material participation (for example, making management decisions such as approving tenants and setting rents).

Working interests in oil and gas properties are excluded from the passive activity rules by §469(c)(3) regardless of participation. Activities in which the taxpayer materially participates are not passive, and for activities in which the taxpayer does not materially participate the relevant concept is material participation, not active participation.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産活動に積極的に関与（active participation）する個人は、その活動のパッシブ損失のうち最大$25,000を非パッシブ所得と通算できる（修正AGI $100,000〜$150,000で段階的に縮小）。積極的関与は、入居者の承認や賃料設定などの経営判断への関与で足り、実質的関与（material participation）より緩い基準である。

石油・ガスの作業権益（working interest）は関与の程度にかかわらずパッシブ活動から除外される（§469(c)(3)）。実質的に関与している活動はそもそもパッシブではなく、実質的に関与していない活動で問題となるのは実質的関与の有無であり、積極的関与ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Sanderson has made deductible contributions to his traditional IRA for many years. Sanderson recently retired at age 60 and received a distribution of $150,000. In which way, if any, will the distribution be taxed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a capital gain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: As ordinary income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Subject to a 10% penalty.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It will not be taxed.

questions.explanation:
Distributions from a traditional IRA are included in gross income as ordinary income under IRC §408(d)(1) and §72, to the extent they exceed any nondeductible contributions (basis). Because all of Sanderson's contributions were deductible, he has no basis and the entire $150,000 is ordinary income.

IRA distributions are not capital gains, even if the account held capital assets. The 10% additional tax on early distributions under §72(t) does not apply because Sanderson is over age 59½. The distribution is not tax-free; only qualified distributions from a Roth IRA are excluded.
questions.explanationJa:
従来型IRAからの分配は、控除されなかった拠出額（basis）を超える部分が通常所得として総所得に算入される（IRC §408(d)(1)、§72）。Sandersonの拠出はすべて控除済みなのでbasisはなく、$150,000全額が通常所得となる。

IRA内で資本資産を運用していてもIRAの分配はキャピタルゲインにならない。60歳であり59½歳を超えているので、§72(t)の早期分配に対する10%の追加税はかからない。非課税となるのはRoth IRAの適格分配のみであり、本問の分配は課税される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Which of the following would qualify as a deductible charitable contribution in year 1 for an individual taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A $200 contribution to the taxpayer's church charged by credit card on December 31, year 1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A $450 contribution to a senator's campaign on December 31, year 1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A $1,000 contribution to a foreign charity on December 31, year 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A contribution on December 31, year 1, of $500 worth of clothing to the Salvation Army for which substantiation was not obtained.

questions.explanation:
A charitable contribution charged to a credit card is treated as paid in the year it is charged, even though the card balance is paid later (Rev. Rul. 78-38). A church is a qualified organization under IRC §170(c)(2), so the $200 charged on December 31 of year 1 is deductible in year 1.

Contributions to a political campaign are not made to a §170(c) organization and are not deductible. Contributions to a foreign charity are not deductible because §170(c)(2) requires the organization to be created or organized in the United States. A noncash contribution of $250 or more, such as the $500 of clothing, requires a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the donee under §170(f)(8); without that substantiation no deduction is allowed.
questions.explanationJa:
クレジットカードで支払った寄附は、カード代金を後で支払う場合でもカードで決済した年に支払ったものとされる（Rev. Rul. 78-38）。教会はIRC §170(c)(2)の適格団体なので、year 1の12月31日にカード決済した$200はyear 1に控除できる。

選挙運動への献金は§170(c)の団体への寄附ではないので控除できない。外国の慈善団体への寄附は、§170(c)(2)が米国で設立された団体であることを求めているため控除できない。$250以上の現物寄附（$500の衣類）は§170(f)(8)により受贈団体の書面による受領証明が必要で、それがなければ控除は認められない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.31 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Bartlet owns a manufacturing business and participates in the business. Which of the following conditions would cause the business to be considered a nonpassive activity for Bartlet?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bartlet participates in the business for more than 500 hours during a year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The business made a profit in any three of the last five years that preceded the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The business has at least 10 employees who, individually or collectively, work for the business more than 1,000 hours in a year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bartlet files an election with the IRS postponing nonpassive activity classification.

questions.explanation:
A trade or business is a nonpassive activity for a taxpayer who materially participates in it (IRC §469(c)(1), (h)(1)). Under Treas. Reg. §1.469-5T(a)(1), an individual materially participates if the individual participates in the activity for more than 500 hours during the year.

Having a profit in three of the last five years is the §183(d) presumption that an activity is engaged in for profit (hobby loss rules), not a material participation test. Hours worked by employees do not count toward the owner's participation. There is no election to postpone or choose nonpassive classification; status depends on the taxpayer's own participation.
questions.explanationJa:
納税者が実質的に関与（material participation）している事業は非パッシブ活動となる（IRC §469(c)(1)、(h)(1)）。Treas. Reg. §1.469-5T(a)(1)では、個人がその年に500時間を超えて活動に参加していれば実質的関与に当たる。

過去5年のうち3年で利益が出ていることは、§183(d)の営利目的の推定（趣味損失のルール）であり、実質的関与の基準ではない。従業員の作業時間は所有者の関与時間に算入されない。非パッシブとする区分を延期・選択する届出制度もなく、本人の関与で判断される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: Juan recently started operating a flower shop as a proprietorship. In its first year of operations, the shop had a taxable income of $60,000. Assuming that Juan had no other employment-related earnings,

choices.label: A
choices.text: The flower shop must withhold FICA taxes from Juan's earnings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Juan must pay self-employment tax on the earnings of the business.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Juan will be exempt from self-employment taxes for the first three years of operations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Juan will be exempt from the Medicare tax because the business earnings are below the threshold amount.

questions.explanation:
A sole proprietor is not an employee of the business, so no FICA tax is withheld from the proprietor's earnings. Instead, IRC §1401 imposes self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare) on net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more (§1402(b)). Juan's $60,000 of business income is therefore subject to self-employment tax, computed on 92.35% of net earnings.

A proprietorship does not withhold FICA from its owner. There is no exemption from self-employment tax for the first three years of a new business. The Medicare portion applies to all net earnings from self-employment with no minimum beyond the $400 filing threshold; the threshold amounts in the law trigger the additional 0.9% Medicare tax, not the basic Medicare tax.
questions.explanationJa:
個人事業主は事業の従業員ではないので、本人の所得からFICA税は源泉徴収されない。代わりにIRC §1401により、自営業による純所得が$400以上（§1402(b)）であれば自営業税（社会保障税・メディケア税）が課される。Juanの事業所得$60,000は自営業税の対象で、純所得の92.35%を基礎に計算する。

個人事業は事業主本人からFICAを源泉徴収しない。開業後3年間の免除制度はない。メディケア部分は自営業の純所得全額にかかり、$400の基準以外に最低額はない。法律上の基準額は0.9%の追加メディケア税の適用基準であり、通常のメディケア税の免除基準ではない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2017 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. null)

questions.stem: A taxpayer received $200 in interest from U.S. Treasury bonds and $300 in interest from municipal bonds. What amount of interest should be included in the taxpayer's gross income?
questions.explanation:
Interest on U.S. Treasury bonds is included in federal gross income under IRC §61(a)(4) (it is exempt only from state and local income taxes). Interest on municipal (state and local) bonds is excluded from federal gross income under §103(a).

Gross income = $200 Treasury interest

The $300 amount includes the municipal interest instead of the Treasury interest, which reverses the rules. The $500 amount includes both, and the $0 amount excludes both.
questions.explanationJa:
米国財務省債の利息は連邦の総所得に含まれる（IRC §61(a)(4)。州・地方の所得税だけが非課税）。地方債（州・地方政府債）の利息は§103(a)により連邦の総所得から除外される。

総所得 = 財務省債の利息$200

$300は財務省債ではなく地方債の利息を含めており、規定が逆である。$500は両方を含め、$0は両方を除外している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.9 (AICPA No. 62577)

questions.stem:
A married couple reported the following items for the current year:

Salaries | $95,000
Dividends | 1,000
Interest income on savings account | 500
Loss from rental real estate | (2,000)

Both spouses actively participate in the rental real estate activities. What is the taxpayers' adjusted gross income on a joint return for the year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(i), taxpayers who actively participate in rental real estate may deduct up to $25,000 of rental losses against nonpassive income. The allowance is reduced by 50% of modified AGI over $100,000. Modified AGI is computed without the passive loss: $95,000 + $1,000 + $500 = $96,500, which is below $100,000, so the full $2,000 loss is deductible.

Salaries = $95,000
Dividends = $1,000
Interest = $500
Rental real estate loss = ($2,000)
AGI = $94,500

The $95,000 amount reports only salaries, and the $96,500 amount omits the deductible rental loss. The $98,500 amount adds the loss instead of subtracting it.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(i)により、賃貸不動産に積極的に関与する納税者は、賃貸損失のうち最大$25,000を非パッシブ所得と通算できる。この枠は修正AGIが$100,000を超える部分の50%だけ減額される。修正AGIはパッシブ損失を除いて計算し、$95,000 + $1,000 + $500 = $96,500 で$100,000未満なので、$2,000の損失全額を控除できる。

給与 = $95,000
配当 = $1,000
利息 = $500
賃貸不動産の損失 = ($2,000)
AGI = $94,500

$95,000は給与だけ、$96,500は控除できる賃貸損失を差し引いていない額。$98,500は損失を差し引かずに加えている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.10 (AICPA No. 63041)

questions.stem: Four years ago, when Cox's spouse died, Cox filed a joint tax return for that year. Cox did not remarry, but continued to provide full support for a minor child who has been living with Cox. What is Cox's most advantageous filing status for the current year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Single.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Married filing separate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Surviving spouse.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Head of household.

questions.explanation:
A qualifying surviving spouse (IRC §2(a)) may use joint return rates only for the two tax years following the year of the spouse's death, and only while maintaining a home for a dependent child. Cox's spouse died four years ago, so that period has expired. Cox is unmarried and maintains a household for a minor child who lives with Cox and whom Cox fully supports, so Cox qualifies as head of household under §2(b), which has more favorable rates and a larger standard deduction than single status.

Single status is available but less advantageous than head of household. Married filing separately is not available to an unmarried individual. Surviving spouse status no longer applies because more than two years have passed since the year of death.
questions.explanationJa:
適格生存配偶者（IRC §2(a)）として共同申告の税率を使えるのは、配偶者が死亡した年の翌2年間で、扶養する子と住居を維持している場合に限られる。Coxの配偶者は4年前に死亡しているので、その期間は終わっている。Coxは未婚で、同居する未成年の子を全面的に扶養して世帯を維持しているので、§2(b)の世帯主（head of household）に該当し、独身より有利な税率と大きい標準控除を使える。

独身（single）でも申告できるが、世帯主より不利である。未婚者は夫婦個別申告を選べない。死亡年から2年を超えているので、生存配偶者の資格はもう使えない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.11 (AICPA No. 60741)

questions.stem: A painter and an accountant agree to trade their services. The painter provides services valued at $550, and the accountant provides services worth $500. What amount should the accountant report as income or expense?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $50 expense.

choices.label: B
choices.text: $50 income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: $500 income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: $550 income.

questions.explanation:
In a barter transaction, each party must include in gross income the fair market value of the property or services received (IRC §61(a); Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1)). The accountant received painting services worth $550, so the accountant reports $550 of income.

Income = FMV of services received = $550

The $500 income amount is the value of the services the accountant provided, not the value received. Reporting a $50 expense or $50 income nets the two values against each other, but barter income is not netted; the full value received is income.
questions.explanationJa:
物々交換（バーター取引）では、各当事者は受け取った財産・役務の時価を総所得に含める（IRC §61(a)、Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1)）。会計士は時価 $550 の塗装サービスを受け取ったので、$550 を所得として計上する。

$500 の所得は会計士が提供した役務の価値であり、受け取った価値ではない。$50 の費用や $50 の所得は両者の差額で相殺しているが、バーター取引では相殺せず受け取った価値の全額が所得となる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.25 (AICPA No. 65493)

questions.explanation:
A loss on the sale of a personal residence is a nondeductible personal loss (IRC §165(c)) and does not enter the capital gain and loss netting. The municipal bonds, the securities and the investment painting are capital assets, so their gains and losses are netted.

Short-term: municipal bond loss (held seven months) = ($9,000)
Long-term: securities gain $5,000 - painting loss $4,000 = $1,000
Net capital loss = ($9,000) + $1,000 = ($8,000)
Deduction against ordinary income (IRC §1211(b)) = ($3,000)
Carryforward (IRC §1212(b)) = $8,000 - $3,000 = $5,000

The $8,000 amount is the net capital loss before the $3,000 annual deduction. The $16,000 amount incorrectly includes the $11,000 residence loss and then subtracts the $3,000 deduction. The $19,000 amount includes the residence loss and ignores the $3,000 deduction.
questions.explanationJa:
自宅（主たる住居）の売却損は個人的な損失で控除できず（IRC §165(c)）、キャピタルゲイン・ロスの通算にも含めない。地方債・有価証券・投資目的の絵画は資本資産なので通算する。

短期: 地方債の損失（保有7か月） = ($9,000)
長期: 有価証券の利益 $5,000 − 絵画の損失 $4,000 = $1,000
純キャピタルロス = ($8,000)
通常所得からの控除（IRC §1211(b)） = ($3,000)
繰越額（IRC §1212(b)） = $8,000 − $3,000 = $5,000

$8,000 は年 $3,000 の控除を差し引く前の純損失。$16,000 は自宅の損失 $11,000 を含めたうえで $3,000 を控除した額、$19,000 は自宅の損失を含め $3,000 の控除も無視した額で、いずれも誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2018 Recently Released Q.27 (AICPA No. 60745)

questions.stem: An individual acquired 500 shares of stock on December 20, year 1, for a personal portfolio. On March 15, year 2, the individual executed a short sale of 500 shares of the stock. On December 21, year 2, the individual delivered the 500 shares to cover the short sale. Which of the following statements best characterizes the gain or loss on the short sale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as ordinary income because of the March short sale.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as a long-term capital asset sale.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as a 40% short-term/60% long-term capital asset sale.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The transaction will be treated as a short-term capital asset sale.

questions.explanation:
When a taxpayer makes a short sale of stock while holding substantially identical stock that has been held for not more than one year on the date of the short sale, any gain on closing the short sale is short-term, and the holding period of the substantially identical stock begins on the date the short sale is closed (IRC §1233(b)). The shares were acquired December 20, year 1 and the short sale was made March 15, year 2, so they had been held less than one year on the short-sale date. Delivering those shares on December 21, year 2 does not convert the result to long-term.

In addition, if the shares were appreciated, a short sale of the same stock is a constructive sale under IRC §1259 on March 15, year 2, when the holding period was less than one year, which again produces short-term gain.

A short sale of a capital asset does not produce ordinary income. Long-term treatment is incorrect because §1233(b) cuts off the holding period at the short-sale date. The 60% long-term/40% short-term split applies to Section 1256 contracts (such as regulated futures contracts), not to short sales of stock.
questions.explanationJa:
空売りの日に、実質的に同一の株式を保有期間1年以下で保有している場合、空売りの決済による利益は短期となり、その同一株式の保有期間は空売りの決済日から始まる（IRC §1233(b)）。株式の取得は1年目12月20日、空売りは2年目3月15日なので、空売り時点の保有期間は1年未満である。2年目12月21日にその株式を引き渡して決済しても長期にはならない。

さらに株式に含み益がある場合、同じ株式の空売りは IRC §1259 のみなし譲渡（constructive sale）となり、保有期間1年未満の2年目3月15日に譲渡したものとされるため、やはり短期の利益となる。

資本資産の空売りは通常所得にならない。§1233(b) により保有期間が空売り日で区切られるので長期扱いも誤り。長期60%・短期40%の区分は Section 1256 契約（規制先物等）に適用されるもので、株式の空売りには適用されない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.29 (AICPA No. 70255)

questions.stem: A retiree invested $100,000 in an annuity that pays $12,000 annually for 10 years. What portion of the first payment should be included in the retiree's gross income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §72(b), each annuity payment is excluded from gross income in the ratio of the investment in the contract to the expected return under the contract (the exclusion ratio).

Expected return = $12,000 x 10 years = $120,000
Exclusion ratio = $100,000 / $120,000 = 5/6
Excluded portion of each payment = $12,000 x 5/6 = $10,000
Included in gross income = $12,000 - $10,000 = $2,000

The $0 amount treats the whole payment as a recovery of the investment until it is fully recovered, which is not the annuity rule. The $10,000 amount is the excluded portion, not the taxable portion. The $12,000 amount ignores the recovery of the $100,000 investment.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §72(b) により、年金の各受取額のうち「投資額 ÷ 期待受取総額」（除外割合）に相当する部分は総所得から除外される。

期待受取総額 = $12,000 × 10年 = $120,000
除外割合 = $100,000 ÷ $120,000 = 5/6
除外額 = $12,000 × 5/6 = $10,000
総所得に含める額 = $12,000 − $10,000 = $2,000

$0 は投資額を回収し終えるまで全額を元本の回収とみなすもので、年金の規定ではない。$10,000 は除外される部分であり課税部分ではない。$12,000 は投資額 $100,000 の回収を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 63039)

questions.stem: As of December 31, the Mitchells were legally separated and maintained separate households for the entire year. The Mitchells have no children. What filing status should Mr. Mitchell claim for the year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Single.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Head of household.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Married filing separate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Married filing joint.

questions.explanation:
Marital status is determined as of the last day of the tax year. An individual who is legally separated from the spouse under a decree of divorce or of separate maintenance is not considered married (IRC §7703(a)(2)). Mr. Mitchell is therefore unmarried at year-end, and because the Mitchells have no children and no qualifying person is described, he files as single.

Head of household status requires maintaining a household for a qualifying person (IRC §2(b)), and there is none. Married filing separately and married filing jointly are available only to taxpayers who are married at year-end, and a legally separated taxpayer is not treated as married.
questions.explanationJa:
婚姻状況は課税年度の末日で判定する。離婚判決または別居扶養（separate maintenance）の判決により法的に別居している者は、婚姻しているとはみなされない（IRC §7703(a)(2)）。Mitchell 氏は年末時点で未婚扱いとなり、子どもも適格者もいないため Single で申告する。

Head of household は適格者のための世帯を維持していることが要件で（IRC §2(b)）、該当者がいない。Married filing separate と Married filing joint は年末に婚姻している者だけが使え、法的別居の者は婚姻者として扱われない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.34 (AICPA No. 58111)

questions.stem:
An individual taxpayer's tax return included the following:

Regular tax before tax credits | $5,000
Current-year estimated tax payments | 6,000
Amount paid with current-year extension | 1,000
Federal income tax withheld | 1,000

What amount, if any, is the taxpayer's overpayment?
questions.explanation:
A taxpayer's overpayment is the excess of total payments and credits over the tax liability. Federal income tax withheld is credited against the tax (IRC §31), and estimated tax payments and the amount paid with an extension request are payments of the year's tax. The overpayment may be refunded or credited (IRC §6402).

Total payments = $6,000 + $1,000 + $1,000 = $8,000
Tax liability = $5,000
Overpayment = $8,000 - $5,000 = $3,000

The $0 amount ignores that payments exceed the tax. The $1,000 amount counts only the excess estimated tax payments over the tax liability. The $2,000 amount omits either the withholding or the extension payment.
questions.explanationJa:
過払額は、納付額・税額控除の合計が税額を超える部分である。源泉徴収税額は税額から控除され（IRC §31）、予定納税額と申告期限延長時の納付額もその年の税の納付となる。過払額は還付または充当される（IRC §6402）。

納付額合計 = $6,000 + $1,000 + $1,000 = $8,000
税額 = $5,000
過払額 = $8,000 − $5,000 = $3,000

$0 は納付額が税額を超えていることを無視している。$1,000 は予定納税額と税額の差だけを見ている。$2,000 は源泉徴収額か延長時の納付額のどちらかを漏らしている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2019 Recently Released Q.35 (AICPA No. 65633)

questions.stem: Decker, a 62-year-old single individual, sold his principal residence for the net amount of $500,000 after all selling expenses. Decker bought the house 15 years ago and occupied it until it was sold. On the date of sale, the house had a cost basis of $200,000. Within six months, Decker purchased a new house for $600,000. What amount of gain should Decker recognize from the sale of the residence?
questions.explanation:
IRC §121 allows a taxpayer to exclude up to $250,000 ($500,000 for certain joint filers) of gain on the sale of a principal residence owned and used as the principal residence for at least two of the five years before the sale. Decker owned and occupied the house for 15 years and is single, so the $250,000 limit applies. Age and the purchase of a replacement residence do not affect the exclusion.

Amount realized (net of selling expenses) = $500,000
Adjusted basis = $200,000
Realized gain = $300,000
Exclusion = $250,000
Recognized gain = $300,000 - $250,000 = $50,000

The $0 amount assumes the purchase of a more expensive replacement home defers the gain, a rollover rule that no longer applies. The $175,000 amount subtracts a $125,000 exclusion for taxpayers age 55 or older, which was repealed. The $300,000 amount ignores the §121 exclusion.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §121 により、売却前5年間のうち2年以上所有し主たる住居として使用した自宅の売却益は、$250,000（一定の夫婦合算申告は $500,000）まで除外できる。Decker は15年間所有・居住しており独身なので、上限は $250,000。年齢や買換え住宅の購入は除外額に影響しない。

譲渡対価（売却費用控除後）$500,000 − 取得価額 $200,000 = 実現利得 $300,000
除外額 $250,000 → 認識利得 $50,000

$0 は高額な住宅への買換えで利得が繰り延べられるとする旧制度の考え方で、現在は適用されない。$175,000 は廃止された55歳以上の $125,000 除外を差し引いている。$300,000 は §121 の除外を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.14 (AICPA No. 57753)

questions.stem: Decker, an individual, owns 100% of Acre, an S corporation. At the beginning of the year, Decker's basis in Acre was $25,000.
