Acre had ordinary income during the year in the amount of $10,000 and a long-term capital loss in the amount of $4,000. Decker has no other capital gains or losses during the year. What amount of the long-term capital loss may Decker deduct this year?
questions.explanation:
An S corporation's long-term capital loss is a separately stated item that passes through to the shareholder (IRC §1366(a)). Decker's basis ($25,000 + $10,000 of ordinary income = $35,000) exceeds the $4,000 loss, so basis does not limit it. However, at the individual level, net capital losses are deductible against ordinary income only up to $3,000 per year (IRC §1211(b)); because Decker has no other capital gains, $3,000 is deductible and the remaining $1,000 is carried forward (IRC §1212(b)).

Pass-through long-term capital loss = $4,000
Deductible this year = $3,000
Carryforward = $1,000

The $0 amount wrongly treats the loss as nondeductible. The $1,000 amount is the carryforward, not the deduction. The $4,000 amount ignores the $3,000 annual limit on net capital losses.
questions.explanationJa:
S法人の長期キャピタルロスは区分記載項目として株主に配賦される（IRC §1366(a)）。Decker の basis（$25,000 + 通常所得 $10,000 = $35,000）は損失 $4,000 を上回るので basis による制限はない。しかし個人段階では、純キャピタルロスを通常所得から控除できるのは年 $3,000 までで（IRC §1211(b)）、他にキャピタルゲインがないため $3,000 を控除し、残り $1,000 は繰り越す（IRC §1212(b)）。

$0 は損失を控除できないとしており誤り。$1,000 は繰越額であって当年の控除額ではない。$4,000 は年 $3,000 の上限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.17 (AICPA No. 57985)

questions.stem:
West is single, has no dependents, and does not itemize. West provides the following information regarding his current-year's return:

Long-term capital gain | $15,000
Percentage depletion in excess of basis | 9,000
Dividends from publicly-held companies | 10,000

What is the amount of West's AMT tax preference items?
questions.explanation:
Tax preference items under IRC §57 are added to taxable income in computing alternative minimum taxable income. Percentage depletion in excess of the adjusted basis of the property is a tax preference item (IRC §57(a)(1)). Long-term capital gains and qualified dividends are not preference items; they are included in both regular taxable income and AMTI and retain their preferential rates under AMT (IRC §55(b)(3)).

Tax preference items = excess percentage depletion = $9,000

The $19,000 amount adds the $10,000 of dividends, and the $24,000 amount adds the $15,000 long-term capital gain; neither is a preference item. The $34,000 amount treats all three items as preferences.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §57 の tax preference items は、代替ミニマム課税所得（AMTI）の計算で課税所得に加算する項目である。資産の取得価額を超えるパーセンテージ減耗控除は tax preference item に当たる（IRC §57(a)(1)）。長期キャピタルゲインや適格配当は preference item ではなく、通常の課税所得にも AMTI にも含まれ、AMT でも軽減税率が維持される（IRC §55(b)(3)）。

tax preference items = 取得価額を超える減耗控除 $9,000

$19,000 は配当 $10,000 を、$24,000 は長期キャピタルゲイン $15,000 を加えているが、どちらも preference item ではない。$34,000 は3項目すべてを preference としている。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part1 Q.18 (AICPA No. 59045)

questions.stem:
The following year-1 annual report was received by Clark from the qualified-defined contribution plan provided by Clark's employer:

Beginning balance | $12,700
Employer contribution | 600
Plan earnings | 250
Ending balance | $13,550

What income must be included in Clark's gross income for year 1?
questions.explanation:
Employer contributions to a qualified defined contribution plan and the earnings on plan assets are not taxed to the employee when contributed or earned. The plan trust is tax-exempt (IRC §501(a)), and amounts are included in the employee's gross income only when actually distributed (IRC §402(a)). Clark received no distribution in year 1, so gross income from the plan is $0.

The $250 amount incorrectly taxes the plan earnings currently. The $600 amount incorrectly taxes the employer contribution currently. The $850 amount ($600 + $250) incorrectly taxes the entire increase in the account balance before any distribution.
questions.explanationJa:
適格確定拠出年金への雇用主拠出額と運用益は、拠出・発生の時点では従業員に課税されない。年金信託は非課税（IRC §501(a)）で、従業員の総所得に算入されるのは実際に分配を受けた時である（IRC §402(a)）。Clarkは1年目に分配を受けていないので、総所得への算入額は$0。

$250は運用益を、$600は雇用主拠出額を、$850（$600 + $250）は残高増加額の全部を、分配前に課税してしまっている点で誤り。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.11 (AICPA No. 62517)

questions.stem:
An individual partner received a Schedule K-1 from a partnership for year 2 reporting the following items:

Ordinary business income | $45,000
Interest income | 8,000
Net Section 1231 loss | 5,000
Cash distribution | 6,000

No additional partnership items exist for year 2. What is the total amount from the partnership that will be included in the partner's adjusted gross income on the partner's Form 1040 for year 2?
questions.explanation:
A partner includes his or her distributive share of each partnership item on the partner's own return (IRC §702(a)). Ordinary business income and interest income are included in AGI. A net Section 1231 loss is treated as an ordinary loss (IRC §1231(a)(2)) and is deductible in arriving at AGI. A cash distribution that does not exceed the partner's basis is a nontaxable return of basis (IRC §731(a)) and is not included.

Ordinary business income: $45,000
Plus interest income: + $8,000
Less net Section 1231 loss: - $5,000
Amount included in AGI: $48,000

The $42,000 amount incorrectly subtracts the $6,000 cash distribution as if it reduced income. The $52,000 amount misclassifies the items, treating the Section 1231 loss as an addition and the cash distribution as a reduction ($45,000 + $8,000 + $5,000 - $6,000). The $54,000 amount incorrectly adds the $6,000 cash distribution to the $48,000 of income items.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーは、パートナーシップの各項目の分配割合を自分の申告書に計上する（IRC §702(a)）。通常事業所得と受取利息はAGIに含まれる。Section 1231の純損失は通常損失として扱われ（§1231(a)(2)）、AGIの計算上控除される。持分の税務簿価を超えない現金分配は簿価の回収であり課税されない（§731(a)）。

通常事業所得 $45,000 + 受取利息 $8,000 − Section 1231純損失 $5,000 = $48,000

$42,000は現金分配$6,000を所得から差し引いており誤り。$54,000は現金分配$6,000を所得に加えており誤り。$52,000はSection 1231損失を加算し現金分配を減算する（$45,000 + $8,000 + $5,000 − $6,000）という誤った扱いによる金額である。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.12 (AICPA No. 503817)

questions.stem: In which of the following scenarios would the head of household filing status be available to the taxpayer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single taxpayer maintains a separate home for his parent, who qualifies as a dependent.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A taxpayer with no dependents is the surviving spouse of an individual who died in the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An unmarried taxpayer maintains a household with a 28-year-old son, who earned $10,000 during the tax year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single taxpayer maintains a household that is the principal home for five months of the year for his disabled child.

questions.explanation:
Head of household status requires an unmarried taxpayer (not a surviving spouse) to pay more than half the cost of maintaining a household that is the principal place of abode of a qualifying person for more than half the year (IRC §2(b)). A special rule allows a dependent parent to qualify even if the parent lives in a separate household that the taxpayer maintains (IRC §2(b)(1)). A single taxpayer who maintains a separate home for a parent who qualifies as a dependent therefore may file as head of household.

A taxpayer with no dependents whose spouse died in the current year is treated as married for that year and may file a joint return; with no qualifying person, head of household is not available. A 28-year-old son is too old to be a qualifying child (IRC §152(c)(3)), and his $10,000 of earnings exceeds the gross income limit for a qualifying relative (IRC §152(d)(1)), so he is not a qualifying person. A disabled child who lives in the household for only five months does not share the taxpayer's principal home for more than half the year.
questions.explanationJa:
世帯主（head of household）の申告資格は、未婚の納税者が、適格者（qualifying person）の主たる住居である家計の維持費用の半分超を負担し、その者が年の半分超同居していることが要件である（IRC §2(b)）。扶養親族である親については特例があり、納税者が維持する別の住居に住んでいても適格者となる（§2(b)(1)）。したがって、扶養親族の親のために別の住居を維持する単身者は世帯主で申告できる。

扶養親族がおらず配偶者が当年に死亡した納税者は、その年は既婚として共同申告ができるが、適格者がいないため世帯主にはなれない。28歳の息子は年齢要件により qualifying child にならず、所得$10,000は qualifying relative の総所得基準を超えるため適格者にならない。障害のある子が同居したのが5か月だけでは、年の半分超の同居要件を満たさない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.14 (AICPA No. 98170)

questions.stem: A partner in a real estate partnership had a basis of $5,000 at the beginning of the year and a basis of $10,000 at year end. The partner's at-risk amount at year end was $8,000. The partner's Form K-1 listed $12,000 as the partner's share of the partnership's ordinary loss. What amount can the partner deduct on the partner's tax return?
questions.explanation:
A partner's share of partnership loss must pass two limitations in order: the basis limitation (IRC §704(d)) and then the at-risk limitation (IRC §465).

Share of ordinary loss: $12,000
Basis limitation: the year-end basis of $10,000 limits the loss to $10,000.
At-risk limitation: the at-risk amount of $8,000 further limits the loss to $8,000.
Deductible loss: $8,000 (the remaining $4,000 is carried forward under the basis and at-risk rules).

The $5,000 amount uses the beginning-of-year basis, but the loss limitation is applied using basis at the end of the year after current-year increases. The $10,000 amount stops at the basis limitation and ignores the at-risk limitation. The $12,000 amount ignores both limitations.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーシップ損失の配分額は、まず持分簿価の制限（IRC §704(d)）、次にat-risk制限（§465）の順に判定する。

通常損失の配分額 $12,000
簿価制限: 年度末の簿価$10,000が上限 → $10,000
at-risk制限: at-risk額$8,000が上限 → $8,000
控除できる損失: $8,000（残る$4,000は翌年以降に繰り越す）

$5,000は期首の簿価を使っているが、損失制限は当期の増加を反映した年度末の簿価で判定する。$10,000は簿価制限だけでat-risk制限を無視している。$12,000は両方の制限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2020 Recently Released Part2 Q.34 (AICPA No. 76307)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about treatment of net passive activity losses of an individual is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Passive activity losses in excess of passive activity income are permanently disallowed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Net passive activity losses can be offset against portfolio income in the current year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Net passive activity losses are suspended and carried forward to offset passive income of future years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A taxpayer can elect either to offset net passive activity losses against active and portfolio income or to carry the losses forward to future years.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §469(a), a passive activity loss (passive losses in excess of passive income) is not allowed in the current year. The disallowed loss is not lost; it is suspended and carried forward indefinitely to be treated as a passive deduction in the next year (IRC §469(b)), where it may offset passive income. Any remaining suspended loss is allowed in full when the taxpayer disposes of the entire interest in the activity in a fully taxable transaction (IRC §469(g)).

Passive losses are not permanently disallowed; they carry forward. Net passive losses cannot offset portfolio income (interest, dividends, capital gains on investments) or active income. There is no election to offset net passive losses against active and portfolio income.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §469(a)により、パッシブ活動損失（パッシブ損失がパッシブ所得を超える部分）は当年には控除できない。否認された損失は消滅せず、繰り越されて翌年以降のパッシブ控除として扱われ（§469(b)）、将来のパッシブ所得と相殺できる。その活動の持分全部を課税取引で処分した時点で、残っている繰越損失は全額控除できる（§469(g)）。

パッシブ損失は永久に否認されるのではなく繰り越される。純パッシブ損失はポートフォリオ所得（利子・配当・投資の譲渡益）や能動的所得とは相殺できない。能動的所得・ポートフォリオ所得と相殺するか繰り越すかを選択する制度もない。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.12 (AICPA No. 62995)

questions.stem:
A taxpayer reported the following in a tax year:

Salary | $122,000
Capital gain dividends | 3,700
Partnership short-term capital loss | (6,300)

The taxpayer acquired the partnership interest during the year in exchange for a capital contribution of $2,750, and there were no additional items affecting the taxpayer's basis in the partnership. What is the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the year?
questions.explanation:
A partner's distributive share of partnership loss is allowed only to the extent of the partner's adjusted basis in the partnership interest at the end of the year (IRC §704(d)). The allowed portion of the short-term capital loss is then netted with the taxpayer's other capital gains.

Basis in the partnership interest: $2,750 (capital contribution; no other basis items).
Allowable share of the partnership short-term capital loss: $2,750 (the remaining $3,550 is suspended).
Net capital gain: $3,700 capital gain dividends - $2,750 = $950.
AGI: $122,000 salary + $950 = $122,950.

The $119,400 amount ($122,000 + $3,700 - $6,300) deducts the full partnership loss without applying the basis limitation. The $122,000 amount omits both the capital gain dividends and the allowable loss. The $122,700 amount ($122,000 + $3,700 - $3,000) applies the $3,000 capital loss limit, which applies only to a net capital loss; here the allowable loss of $2,750 is fully absorbed by the $3,700 capital gain.
questions.explanationJa:
パートナーシップ損失の配分額は、年度末の持分の税務簿価の範囲でしか控除できない（IRC §704(d)）。控除できる短期資本損失を、その他のキャピタルゲインと通算する。

持分の簿価: $2,750（出資額。他の調整なし）
控除できる短期資本損失: $2,750（残り$3,550は繰越）
純キャピタルゲイン: キャピタルゲイン配当$3,700 − $2,750 = $950
AGI: 給与$122,000 + $950 = $122,950

$119,400（$122,000 + $3,700 − $6,300）は簿価制限を適用せず損失全額を控除している。$122,000はキャピタルゲイン配当と控除可能損失の両方を除外している。$122,700（$122,000 + $3,700 − $3,000）は$3,000の資本損失控除上限を当てはめているが、この上限は純資本損失がある場合の規定であり、本問では控除可能な$2,750は$3,700の利得の中で全額通算される。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.30 (AICPA No. 502563)

questions.stem: Which of the following taxpayers would not qualify for the filing status of head of household?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single taxpayer whose spouse died in the preceding tax year and who has a dependent child living in the household.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A married taxpayer with a dependent child in the household who has lived apart from the taxpayer's spouse for the entire year due to abandonment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single taxpayer who provides over one-half of the support for a dependent parent in a nursing home but does not have a qualifying child in the household.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A single taxpayer who provides one-half of the support for a dependent child who has lived almost the entire year at a U.S. university while pursuing an undergraduate degree.

questions.explanation:
A taxpayer whose spouse died in either of the two preceding tax years and who maintains a household for a dependent child qualifies as a surviving spouse (qualifying surviving spouse) under IRC §2(a). An individual who is a surviving spouse is excluded from head of household status (IRC §2(b)(1)), so the single taxpayer whose spouse died in the preceding year and who has a dependent child in the household would not file as head of household; that taxpayer uses the more favorable qualifying surviving spouse status.

A married taxpayer who maintains a home for a dependent child and whose spouse has not lived in the home during the last six months of the year is treated as unmarried (IRC §7703(b)) and may file as head of household. A dependent parent need not live with the taxpayer; maintaining the parent's home, including a nursing home, qualifies (IRC §2(b)(1)). A dependent child who is away at a university is temporarily absent and is treated as living in the taxpayer's household.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者が前2年以内に死亡し、扶養する子のために家計を維持する納税者は、IRC §2(a)の qualifying surviving spouse に該当する。surviving spouse に当たる者は世帯主の資格から除外される（§2(b)(1)）ため、前年に配偶者を亡くし扶養する子と同居する単身者は世帯主では申告せず、より有利な qualifying surviving spouse で申告する。

扶養する子のために家計を維持し、年の後半6か月間配偶者が同居していない既婚者は未婚とみなされ（§7703(b)）、世帯主で申告できる。扶養する親は同居不要で、介護施設を含む親の住居を維持すれば足りる（§2(b)(1)）。大学に通うため家を離れている扶養する子は一時的不在として同居扱いになる。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.31 (AICPA No. 502131)

questions.stem: Which of the following can be subject to the net investment income tax?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An individual who is a resident of the U.S.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A domestic C corporation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A nonresident alien.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A trust whose unexpired interests are devoted to a charitable purpose.

questions.explanation:
The 3.8% net investment income tax applies to individuals, estates, and trusts (IRC §1411(a)). An individual who is a U.S. citizen or resident is subject to the tax on the lesser of net investment income or modified AGI in excess of the threshold amount.

The tax does not apply to corporations, so a domestic C corporation is not subject to it. Nonresident aliens are expressly excluded (IRC §1411(e)(1)). Trusts all of whose unexpired interests are devoted to charitable purposes are excluded by regulation (Treas. Reg. §1.1411-3(b)).
questions.explanationJa:
3.8%の純投資所得税（NIIT）は個人・遺産財団・信託に課される（IRC §1411(a)）。米国市民または居住者である個人は、純投資所得と、修正AGIのうち基準額を超える部分のいずれか少ない額に対して課税される。

法人には適用されないので、国内C法人は対象外。非居住外国人は明文で除外されている（§1411(e)(1)）。未経過の権利がすべて慈善目的に充てられる信託は、規則で除外されている（Treas. Reg. §1.1411-3(b)）。
questions.source: Proactive AICPA過去問DB REG 2021 Recently Released Q.32 (AICPA No. 77052)

questions.stem:
Barkley owns a vacation cabin that was rented to unrelated parties for 10 days during the year for $2,500. The cabin was used personally by Barkley for three months and left vacant for the rest of the year. Expenses for the cabin were as follows:

Expense | Amount
Real estate taxes | $1,000
Maintenance and utilities | $2,000

How much rental income (loss) is included in Barkley's adjusted gross income?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §280A(g), if a dwelling unit used by the taxpayer as a residence is rented for fewer than 15 days during the year, the rental income is excluded from gross income and no rental expenses are deductible against it. Barkley rented the cabin for only 10 days and used it personally for three months, so the $2,500 of rent is not reported and the rental activity produces neither income nor loss.
Rental income (loss) included in AGI = $0.
The $1,000 of real estate taxes may still be claimed as an itemized deduction (subject to the SALT limitation), but that is below the line and does not create a rental loss; the maintenance and utilities are personal and nondeductible.
The $500 amount nets the rent against the $2,000 of maintenance and utilities, and the $(500) amount nets the rent against all $3,000 of expenses; both ignore the 14-day exclusion rule. The $(1,500) loss is also wrong because a rental of fewer than 15 days can never generate a deductible rental loss.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §280A(g) により、自己が住居として使用する物件の賃貸日数が年14日以下の場合、賃貸収入は総所得から除外され、賃貸に係る費用も控除できません。Barkley の賃貸は10日だけで、3か月は自己使用しているため、$2,500 の賃料は申告せず、賃貸による所得も損失も生じません。
AGI に含まれる賃貸所得（損失）＝$0。
固定資産税 $1,000 は項目別控除（SALT 上限の範囲内）として控除できますが、AGI の計算外であり賃貸損失にはなりません。維持費・光熱費は個人的費用で控除不可です。
$500 は賃料から維持費・光熱費 $2,000 を差し引いた額、$(500) は費用 $3,000 全額を差し引いた額で、いずれも14日ルールを無視しています。$(1,500) の損失も、14日以下の賃貸では賃貸損失が生じないため誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.1

questions.stem:
Chris Baker's adjusted gross income on her Year 1 tax return was $160,000. The amount covered a 12-month period. For Year 2, Baker may avoid the penalty for the underpayment of estimated tax if the timely estimated tax payments equal the required annual amount of

I. 110% of the tax on the return for the last year, paid in four equal installments
II. 100% of prior year's tax liability, paid in four equal installments

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §6654(d)(1), an individual avoids the underpayment penalty by paying the lesser of 90% of the current-year tax or 100% of the prior-year tax (if the prior year was a full 12-month year with a return filed). IRC §6654(d)(1) raises the prior-year percentage to 110% when prior-year AGI exceeds $150,000 ($75,000 if married filing separately).
Baker's Year 1 AGI of $160,000 exceeds $150,000, so the prior-year safe harbor requires 110% of the Year 1 tax, paid in four equal installments.
Paying 100% of the prior year's liability is not enough for a taxpayer above the $150,000 AGI threshold, so the statement in II does not provide protection; that also rules out the both and neither responses.
questions.explanationJa:
個人の見積納税の過少納付ペナルティは、当年税額の90%か前年税額の100%（前年が12か月で申告済みの場合）の少ない方を納付すれば回避できます（IRC §6654(d)(1)）。ただし前年 AGI が $150,000（夫婦個別申告は $75,000）を超える場合、前年基準は110%に引き上げられます（IRC §6654(d)(1)）。
Baker の Year 1 の AGI は $160,000 で $150,000 を超えるため、前年基準を使うには前年税額の110%を4回均等に納付する必要があります。
前年税額の100%では足りないため II は当たらず、「両方」「どちらでもない」も誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.8

questions.stem:
A CPA's adjusted gross income (AGI) for the preceding 12-month tax year exceeds $150,000. Which of the following methods is (are) available to the CPA to compute the required annual payment of estimated tax for the current year in order to make timely estimated tax payments and avoid the underpayment of estimated tax penalty?

I. The annualization method
II. The seasonal method

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
An individual may use the annualized income installment method of IRC §6654(d)(2), which computes each required installment based on income actually earned through the end of each period. It is available to any individual regardless of AGI; the $150,000 AGI threshold only changes the prior-year safe harbor from 100% to 110% (IRC §6654(d)(1)).
A seasonal method (the adjusted seasonal installment method) exists only for corporations under IRC §6655(e)(3), so it is not available to an individual CPA. Therefore II is not available, which also rules out the both and neither responses.
questions.explanationJa:
個人は IRC §6654(d)(2) の年換算所得法（annualized income installment method）を使え、各期末までに実際に稼得した所得に基づいて各回の納付額を計算できます。これは AGI に関係なく使え、AGI $150,000 超で変わるのは前年基準が100%から110%になる点だけです（IRC §6654(d)(1)）。
季節調整法（adjusted seasonal installment method）は IRC §6655(e)(3) の法人専用の方法で、個人の CPA は使えません。したがって II は当たらず、「両方」「どちらでもない」も誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.10

questions.stem:
Alternative minimum tax preferences include the following items. The second item refers to charitable contributions.

Tax-exempt private activity bond interest | Gifts of appreciated capital gain property

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | No

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §57(a)(5), interest on specified private activity bonds that is exempt from regular tax is a tax preference item added back in computing alternative minimum taxable income (bonds issued in 2009 and 2010 are excepted).
The untaxed appreciation on charitable contributions of appreciated capital gain property was formerly a preference, but it was repealed by the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1993; the fair market value deduction is now allowed in full for AMT purposes.
Therefore private activity bond interest is a preference (Yes) and gifts of appreciated capital gain property are not (No). Treating both as preferences, neither as a preference, or only the charitable gift as a preference misstates the current AMT rules.
questions.explanationJa:
通常の所得税で非課税となる特定私的活動債（private activity bonds）の利子は、IRC §57(a)(5) により AMT の優遇項目（preference）として AMTI に加算されます（2009・2010年発行分は除く）。
値上がりしたキャピタルゲイン資産の寄附による含み益は、かつては優遇項目でしたが1993年の OBRA で廃止され、AMT でも時価による控除がそのまま認められます。
したがって私的活動債の利子は Yes、値上がり資産の寄附は No です。両方 Yes、両方 No、寄附だけ Yes の組み合わせはいずれも現行の AMT の扱いと一致しません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.12

questions.stem: The credit for prior year alternative minimum tax liability may be carried

choices.label: A
choices.text: Forward for a maximum of 5 years

choices.label: B
choices.text: Back to the 3 preceding years or carried forward for a maximum of 5 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Back to the 3 preceding years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Forward indefinitely

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §53, the minimum tax credit equals the AMT attributable to deferral items in prior years. It is allowed in a later year only to the extent the regular tax exceeds the tentative minimum tax, and any unused credit carries forward indefinitely until used. There is no carryback.
A 5-year limit on the carryforward, a carryback to the 3 preceding years, and a combination of the two all misstate IRC §53, which has no carryback and no expiration.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §53 の最低税額控除（minimum tax credit）は、過年度の AMT のうち繰延項目（減価償却の差異など）に起因する部分について認められます。後の年度に通常税額が暫定最低税額を超える範囲で使用でき、未使用分は使い切るまで無期限に繰り越せます。繰戻しはありません。
繰越5年まで、3年繰戻し、両者の組み合わせは、繰戻しがなく期限もない IRC §53 の規定と一致しません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.13

questions.stem: The alternative minimum tax (AMT) is computed as the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excess of the tentative minimum tax over the regular tax

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess of the regular tax liability over the tentative minimum tax

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tentative minimum tax plus the regular tax

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lesser of the tentative minimum tax or the regular tax

questions.explanation:
IRC §55(a) imposes the alternative minimum tax equal to the excess (if any) of the tentative minimum tax over the regular tax for the year. The taxpayer pays the regular tax plus this excess, so total tax equals the greater of the two amounts.
The excess of the regular tax over the tentative minimum tax is the amount that limits the minimum tax credit, not the AMT. Adding the full tentative minimum tax to the regular tax would double count, and taking the lesser of the two would make AMT never increase the tax.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §55(a) により、AMT は暫定最低税額（tentative minimum tax）が通常税額を超える額として計算されます。納税者は通常税額にこの超過額を加えて納めるため、結果として両者のうち大きい方を負担します。
通常税額が暫定最低税額を超える額は最低税額控除の使用限度であり AMT ではありません。暫定最低税額の全額を通常税額に足すと二重計算になり、少ない方をとると AMT で税額が増えることがなくなります。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.14

questions.stem: Which of the following credits is a combination of several tax credits to provide uniform rules for the current and carryback-carryover years?

choices.label: A
choices.text: General business credit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foreign tax credit

choices.label: C
choices.text: Minimum tax credit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enhanced oil recovery credit

questions.explanation:
IRC §38 combines a number of separate business credits (for example, the research credit, the work opportunity credit, and the enhanced oil recovery credit) into a single general business credit. The combined credit is subject to one overall limitation based on net income tax, and unused amounts follow uniform carryback (1 year) and carryforward (20 years) rules under IRC §39.
The foreign tax credit is a separate credit under IRC §901 with its own limitation and carryover rules. The minimum tax credit under IRC §53 is a separate credit for prior-year AMT. The enhanced oil recovery credit is one of the components of the general business credit, not the combination itself.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §38 の一般事業税額控除（general business credit）は、研究開発税額控除、就労機会税額控除、石油増進回収税額控除など複数の事業関連の税額控除をまとめたもので、全体に一つの限度額が適用され、未使用分は IRC §39 の統一ルール（1年繰戻し・20年繰越）に従います。
外国税額控除は IRC §901 による別個の控除で独自の限度額・繰越規定があります。最低税額控除は IRC §53 による前年 AMT に係る別の控除です。石油増進回収税額控除は一般事業税額控除の構成要素の一つであり、それ自体が組み合わせではありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.15

questions.stem: Foreign income taxes paid by an individual

choices.label: A
choices.text: May be claimed either as a deduction or as a credit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: May be claimed only as a deduction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: May be claimed only as a credit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Do not qualify either as a deduction or as a credit.

questions.explanation:
Foreign income taxes are deductible as an itemized deduction under IRC §164(a)(3), or the taxpayer may instead elect to claim the foreign tax credit under IRC §901. The choice is made each year, and the taxpayer may not take both for the same taxes (IRC §275(a)(4)). The credit is usually more favorable because it reduces tax dollar for dollar.
Statements limiting the taxes to only a deduction or only a credit ignore the annual election, and the statement that they qualify for neither is wrong because both treatments are permitted.
questions.explanationJa:
外国所得税は IRC §164(a)(3) により項目別控除として所得控除するか、IRC §901 により外国税額控除を選択するかのいずれかで扱えます。選択は毎年行い、同じ税について両方はとれません（IRC §275(a)(4)）。通常は税額を直接減らす税額控除の方が有利です。
「所得控除のみ」「税額控除のみ」は毎年の選択を無視しており、「どちらも不可」は両方の扱いが認められているため誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.16

questions.stem:
To qualify for the child care credit on a joint return, at least one spouse must

Have AGI of $15,000 or less | Be gainfully employed when expenses incurred

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | Yes

questions.explanation:
The child and dependent care credit of IRC §21 has no AGI ceiling for eligibility; AGI only determines the applicable credit percentage, which is highest for taxpayers with AGI of $15,000 or less and declines as AGI rises. So an AGI of $15,000 or less is not required (No).
The expenses must be employment-related, meaning incurred to enable the taxpayer to be gainfully employed, and Treas. Reg. §1.21-1(c) treats expenses incurred while actively searching for work as employment-related. On a joint return the credit is limited by the earned income of the lower-earning spouse, and a spouse who is a full-time student or incapable of self-care is deemed to have earned income (IRC §21(d)(2)). Being gainfully employed at the time the expenses are incurred is therefore not itself the test (No).
The combinations that answer Yes for the $15,000 AGI limit or for employment at the time the expenses are incurred misstate IRC §21.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §21 の子ども・扶養家族の介護費用税額控除には適用要件としての AGI の上限はなく、AGI は控除率を決めるだけです（AGI $15,000 以下で控除率が最も高く、AGI が上がると逓減）。したがって「AGI $15,000 以下」は不要（No）です。
費用は就労関連、すなわち納税者が働けるようにするための費用である必要がありますが、Treas. Reg. §1.21-1(c) は求職活動中に支出した費用も就労関連として扱います。夫婦合算申告では所得の少ない方の配偶者の勤労所得が上限となり、全日制の学生や自活能力のない配偶者は勤労所得があるとみなされます（IRC §21(d)(2)）。費用の支出時点で就業していること自体が要件なのではありません（No）。
AGI 要件や支出時点の就業に Yes と答える組み合わせは、いずれも IRC §21 の規定と一致しません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.17

questions.stem: What can result in a refund even if the individual had no income tax liability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Credit for prior year minimum tax

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elderly and permanently disabled credit

choices.label: C
choices.text: Earned income credit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Child and dependent care credit

questions.explanation:
A refundable credit is paid to the taxpayer even when it exceeds the tax liability. The earned income credit of IRC §32 is refundable (it is treated as an overpayment under IRC §6401(b)), so a qualifying individual with no income tax liability can receive it as a refund.
The credit for prior year minimum tax (IRC §53), the credit for the elderly and permanently disabled (IRC §22), and the child and dependent care credit (IRC §21) are nonrefundable for individuals; they can reduce tax only to zero and cannot produce a refund when there is no liability.
questions.explanationJa:
還付付き税額控除（refundable credit）は、税額を超える部分も納税者に支払われます。IRC §32 の勤労所得税額控除（EIC）は還付付き（IRC §6401(b) で過納付として扱われる）のため、所得税額がゼロの個人でも還付を受けられます。
前年の最低税額控除（IRC §53）、高齢者・障害者税額控除（IRC §22）、子ども・扶養家族の介護費用税額控除（IRC §21）は個人にとって還付なしの控除で、税額をゼロまで減らすだけで、税額がない場合に還付は生じません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.18

questions.stem:
The Sloans paid the following adoption expenses:

Expense | Amount
Child's medical expenses | $5,000
Legal expenses | $8,000
Agency fee | $3,000

How much adoption expenses qualifies for the adoption credit?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §23(d)(1), qualified adoption expenses are reasonable and necessary adoption fees, court costs, attorney fees, and other expenses directly related to the legal adoption of an eligible child. Medical expenses of the child are not adoption expenses.
Qualified expenses = legal expenses $8,000 + agency fee $3,000 = $11,000.
This amount is below the inflation-adjusted dollar limit on the credit, so all $11,000 qualifies.
The $16,000 amount wrongly includes the child's $5,000 of medical expenses, and the $5,000 amount counts only those medical expenses. The $11,650 amount does not correspond to the qualifying legal expenses and agency fee.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §23(d)(1) の適格養子縁組費用は、対象となる子の法的な養子縁組に直接関係する合理的かつ必要な手数料、裁判費用、弁護士費用などです。子の医療費は養子縁組費用に含まれません。
適格費用＝弁護士費用 $8,000＋あっせん機関手数料 $3,000＝$11,000。
この額は物価調整後の控除上限額を下回るため、全額 $11,000 が対象になります。
$16,000 は子の医療費 $5,000 を誤って含め、$5,000 は医療費だけを数えています。$11,650 は適格な弁護士費用と手数料の合計と一致しません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.19

questions.stem: An employee who has social security withheld greater than the maximum for a particular year, may claim

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excess as either a credit or an itemized deduction, at the election of the employee, if excess is from correct withholding by 2 or more employers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reimbursement of such excess from his employers, if excess resulted from correct withholding by 2 or more employers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excess as credit against income tax, if excess resulted from correct withholding by 2 or more employers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Excess as a credit against income tax, if that excess was withheld by one employer.

questions.explanation:
When an employee works for two or more employers and each correctly withholds social security tax on wages up to the annual wage base, the total withheld can exceed the maximum. Under IRC §31(b), the excess is allowed as a credit against the employee's income tax (claimed on Form 1040).
The excess is not deductible, so an election between a credit and an itemized deduction does not exist. Each employer withheld correctly, so neither employer owes a reimbursement. When a single employer over-withholds, the employer must adjust or refund the error; the employee cannot claim that excess as an income tax credit.
questions.explanationJa:
2社以上の雇用主がそれぞれ正しく年間上限額までの賃金に社会保障税を源泉徴収した結果、合計が上限を超えた場合、超過額は IRC §31(b) により所得税からの税額控除として請求できます（Form 1040 で申告）。
超過額は所得控除にはならないため、税額控除と項目別控除の選択はありません。各雇用主は正しく徴収しているので雇用主からの払戻しも受けられません。1社の雇用主が過大に徴収した場合は雇用主が調整・返金すべきもので、従業員が所得税の税額控除として請求することはできません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation (Other Topics) Q.20

questions.stem: A couple filed a joint return in prior tax years. During the current tax year, one spouse died. The couple has no dependent children. What is the filing status available to the surviving spouse for the first subsequent tax year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Surviving spouse

choices.label: B
choices.text: Married filing separately

choices.label: C
choices.text: Single

choices.label: D
choices.text: Head of household

questions.explanation:
In the year of death, the surviving spouse may still file a joint return with the deceased spouse (IRC §6013(a)(2)). For the following years, the qualifying surviving spouse status under IRC §2(a) is available only if the survivor maintains a household for a dependent child or stepchild. Because this couple has no dependent children, the survivor is unmarried and has no qualifying person, so the only status available for the first subsequent year is Single (IRC §1(c)).

Surviving spouse is incorrect because that status requires a dependent child living in the home. Married filing separately is incorrect because the survivor is no longer married after the year of death. Head of household is incorrect because it requires a qualifying person (such as a dependent child or relative) for whom the taxpayer maintains a household.
questions.explanationJa:
配偶者が死亡した年は、生存配偶者は死亡した配偶者と共同申告（joint return）ができます（IRC §6013(a)(2)）。翌年以降の qualifying surviving spouse（適格生存配偶者）は、扶養する子（継子を含む）のために家計を維持していることが条件です（IRC §2(a)）。この夫婦には扶養する子がいないため、翌年の申告区分は Single（独身）になります。

Surviving spouse は扶養する子が要件なので該当しません。Married filing separately は、死亡の翌年には婚姻関係が無いため使えません。Head of household は扶養する適格者が必要なので該当しません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.5

questions.stem: While Emma and John were married, John died on July 1, Year 3. With regard to John's and Emma's filing status for Year 3, Emma should file

choices.label: A
choices.text: As a single individual, and a separate return should be filed for John as unmarried head of household

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a qualifying widow, and a separate return should be filed for John as married head of household

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a qualifying widow, and a separate return should be filed for John as a single deceased individual

choices.label: D
choices.text: A joint return, including John, as married taxpayers

questions.explanation:
Marital status is determined as of the date of death when a spouse dies during the year (IRC §7703(a)(1)). Emma and John are therefore treated as married for all of Year 3, and Emma may file a joint return for Year 3 that includes John's income and deductions, provided she does not remarry before the end of the year (IRC §6013(a)(2)).

Filing as a single individual is incorrect because Emma is considered married for Year 3. Qualifying widow status is incorrect for Year 3 because it applies only to the two years following the year of death and requires a dependent child (IRC §2(a)). A return for John as head of household or as a single deceased individual is also incorrect because John was married on the date of his death.
questions.explanationJa:
年の途中で配偶者が死亡した場合、婚姻状態は死亡日で判定します（IRC §7703(a)(1)）。Emma と John は Year 3 を通じて婚姻中とみなされ、Emma が年末までに再婚しなければ、John を含めた共同申告（joint return）ができます（IRC §6013(a)(2)）。

Emma を独身として申告する案は、Year 3 は婚姻中とされるため誤りです。qualifying widow（適格生存配偶者）は死亡した年の翌年から2年間に限られ、扶養する子も必要なので Year 3 には使えません（IRC §2(a)）。John を head of household や独身の死亡者として申告する案も、死亡日に婚姻中だったため誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.6

questions.stem:
For head of household filing status, which of the following costs are considered in determining whether the taxpayer has contributed more than one half the cost of maintaining the household?

Food consumed in the home | Value of taxpayer's services in the home

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | Yes

questions.explanation:
To qualify as head of household, the taxpayer must furnish over one half of the cost of maintaining the household (IRC §2(b)(1)). Under Treas. Reg. §1.2-2(d), the cost of maintaining a household includes property taxes, mortgage interest, rent, utilities, upkeep and repairs, property insurance, and food consumed on the premises. It does not include clothing, education, medical treatment, vacations, life insurance, transportation, or the value of services rendered in the household by the taxpayer or any member of the household.

So food consumed in the home counts (Yes), and the value of the taxpayer's own services does not count (No). The Yes | Yes combination wrongly counts the taxpayer's services; No | No and No | Yes wrongly exclude food consumed in the home.
questions.explanationJa:
head of household（世帯主）の要件の一つは、家計維持費の半分超を負担していることです（IRC §2(b)(1)）。Treas. Reg. §1.2-2(d) によると、家計維持費には固定資産税、住宅ローン利息、家賃、光熱費、修繕費、保険料、家庭で消費する食費が含まれます。一方、衣服・教育・医療・休暇・生命保険・交通費や、納税者自身や家族が家庭内で提供した役務の価値は含まれません。

したがって食費は Yes、納税者自身の役務の価値は No です。Yes | Yes は役務の価値を含めてしまい、No | No と No | Yes は食費を除いてしまう点が誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.7

questions.stem: Perle, a dentist, billed Wood $600 for dental services. Wood paid Perle $200 cash and built a bookcase for Perle's office in full settlement of the bill. Wood sells comparable bookcases for $350. What amount should Perle include in taxable income as a result of this transaction?
questions.explanation:
Compensation for services is gross income whether received in cash or in property (IRC §61(a)(1)). When services are paid for in property, the fair market value of the property received is included in income (Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1)). The amount billed is irrelevant once Perle accepts the payment in full settlement.

Cash received: $200
Fair market value of the bookcase: $350
Income included: $200 + $350 = $550

The $600 amount is the billed fee, not what Perle actually received. The $200 amount omits the value of the bookcase received in kind, and $0 ignores that barter income is taxable.
questions.explanationJa:
役務の対価は現金でも物でも総所得に含まれます（IRC §61(a)(1)）。物で受け取った場合は、その時価を収入に含めます（Treas. Reg. §1.61-2(d)(1)）。全額の精算として受け取った以上、請求額$600は関係ありません。

現金 $200 ＋ 本棚の時価 $350 ＝ $550

$600 は請求額で、実際に受け取った額ではありません。$200 は現物で受け取った本棚の価値を落としており、$0 は物々交換による所得が課税されることを無視しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.10

questions.stem:
DAC Foundation awarded Kent $75,000 in recognition of lifelong literary achievement. Kent was not required to render future services as a condition to receive the $75,000. What condition(s) must have been met for the award to be excluded from Kent's gross income?
I. Kent was selected for the award by DAC without any action on Kent's part.
II. Pursuant to Kent's designation, DAC paid the amount of the award either to a governmental unit or to a charitable organization.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
Prizes and awards are generally included in gross income (IRC §74(a)). Under IRC §74(b), an award made primarily in recognition of religious, charitable, scientific, educational, artistic, literary, or civic achievement is excluded only if all of the following are met: (1) the recipient was selected without any action on his part to enter the contest or proceeding; (2) the recipient is not required to render substantial future services as a condition of receiving the award; and (3) the award is transferred by the payor to a governmental unit or a charitable organization designated by the recipient.

Kent already meets the no-future-services condition, so both statement I (selection without action) and statement II (payment to a governmental unit or charity at Kent's designation) must also be met. I only and II only each omit a required condition, and Neither I nor II ignores that a literary achievement award paid directly to Kent is taxable.
questions.explanationJa:
賞金・賞品は原則として総所得に含まれます（IRC §74(a)）。宗教・慈善・科学・教育・芸術・文学・市民活動の功績をたたえる賞を非課税にできるのは、IRC §74(b) の3要件をすべて満たす場合だけです。①本人が応募などの行動をせずに選ばれた、②将来の役務提供が受賞の条件でない、③本人の指定に従い支払者が政府機関または慈善団体へ支払った。

Kent は②を満たしているので、I（本人の行動なしに選ばれた）と II（指定先の政府機関・慈善団体への支払）の両方が必要です。I only と II only は要件が欠けており、Neither I nor II は Kent が直接受け取れば課税されることを無視しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.11

questions.stem:
In Year 1, Emily Judd received the following dividends from:

Payor | Amount
Grainte Life Insurance Co., on life policy* | $100
National Bank, on bank's common stock | 300
Roe Mfg. Corp., on preferred stock | 500

* The dividends are on Emily's life insurance policy; total dividends received have not yet exceeded accumulated premiums paid. Roe Mfg. Corp. is a Delaware corporation.

What amount of dividend income should Emily report in her Year 1 income tax return?
questions.explanation:
Dividends on a life insurance policy are treated as a return of premiums, not as dividend income. They are excluded from gross income until the total received exceeds the taxpayer's investment in the contract (IRC §72(e)). Dividends paid by a corporation on its common or preferred stock are gross income (IRC §61(a)(7)).

National Bank common stock dividend: $300
Roe Mfg. Corp. preferred stock dividend: $500
Dividend income: $300 + $500 = $800

The $900 amount wrongly includes the $100 life insurance dividend. The $500 amount omits the bank's common stock dividend, and the $300 amount omits the preferred stock dividend, which is a dividend like any other distribution from earnings and profits.
questions.explanationJa:
生命保険契約の配当は保険料の払戻しとして扱われ、受取累計額が払込保険料（契約への投資額）を超えるまでは非課税です（IRC §72(e)）。法人が普通株・優先株に支払う配当は総所得に含まれます（IRC §61(a)(7)）。

銀行の普通株配当 $300 ＋ Roe社の優先株配当 $500 ＝ $800

$900 は生命保険の配当$100を含めている点が誤りです。$500 は普通株配当を、$300 は優先株配当を落としています。優先株の配当も通常の配当として課税されます。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.12

questions.stem: With regard to the inclusion of social security benefits in gross income, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The social security benefits in excess of modified adjusted gross income are included in gross income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The social security benefits in excess of 85% the modified adjusted gross income are included in gross income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 85% of the social security benefits is the maximum amount of benefits to be included in gross income.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The social security benefits in excess of the modified adjusted gross income over $34,000 are included in gross income.

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §86, the taxable portion of social security benefits depends on provisional income (modified adjusted gross income plus one half of the benefits) compared with base amounts ($25,000 single / $32,000 joint) and adjusted base amounts ($34,000 single / $44,000 joint). Depending on where provisional income falls, 0%, up to 50%, or up to 85% of the benefits are included. In no case is more than 85% of the benefits included in gross income (IRC §86(a)(2)).

The statements that tie the inclusion to benefits in excess of modified adjusted gross income, in excess of 85% of modified adjusted gross income, or in excess of modified adjusted gross income over $34,000 misstate the formula: the inclusion is a percentage of the benefits (or of the excess of provisional income over the base amounts), capped at 85% of the benefits.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §86 では、社会保障給付の課税部分は「暫定所得（修正後AGI＋給付額の1/2）」を基準額（単身$25,000・夫婦合算$32,000）や調整基準額（単身$34,000・夫婦合算$44,000）と比べて決まります。暫定所得の水準に応じて給付の0%、最大50%、最大85%が総所得に入りますが、どの場合でも給付額の85%が上限です（IRC §86(a)(2)）。

「修正後AGIを超える給付」「修正後AGIの85%を超える給付」「$34,000を超える修正後AGIを上回る給付」が算入されるという記述は、いずれも計算の仕組みを取り違えています。算入額は給付額（または暫定所得の基準額超過分）の一定割合で、給付額の85%が上限です。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.13

questions.stem:
In a tax year where the taxpayer pays qualified education expenses, interest income on the redemption of qualified U.S. Series EE Bonds may be excluded from gross income. The exclusion is subject to a modified gross income limitation and a limit of aggregate bond proceeds in excess of qualified higher education expenses. Which of the following is (are) true?
I. The exclusion applies for education expenses incurred by the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse, or any person whom the taxpayer may claim as a dependent for the year.
II. "Otherwise qualified higher education expenses" must be reduced by qualified scholarships not includible in gross income.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
IRC §135 excludes interest on redeemed qualified U.S. savings bonds (such as Series EE bonds) to the extent the redemption proceeds are used for qualified higher education expenses, subject to a modified AGI phase-out.

Statement I is true: qualified higher education expenses are tuition and fees for the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse, or any dependent of the taxpayer (IRC §135(c)(2)).
Statement II is true: the qualified expenses must be reduced by qualified scholarships excludable under §117 and other specified tax-free educational assistance (IRC §135(d)(1)).

Because both statements are true, I only, II only, and Neither I nor II are each incorrect.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §135 は、適格な米国貯蓄債券（Series EE 債など）の償還金を適格高等教育費に充てた場合、その利息を総所得から除外できると定めています（修正後AGIによる段階的縮小あり）。

I は正しい: 対象となる教育費は、納税者本人・配偶者・扶養家族の授業料等です（IRC §135(c)(2)）。
II は正しい: 適格教育費は、§117 で非課税となる奨学金などの非課税の教育援助額だけ減額します（IRC §135(d)(1)）。

どちらも正しいので、I only・II only・Neither I nor II は誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.14

questions.stem: Klein, a master's degree candidate at Briar University, was awarded a $12,000 scholarship from Briar in 2006. The scholarship was used to pay Klein's 2006 university tuition and fees. Also in 2006, Klein received $5,000 for teaching two courses at a nearby college. What amount is includible in Klein's 2006 gross income?
questions.explanation:
A qualified scholarship received by a degree candidate is excluded from gross income to the extent it is used for tuition and required fees, books, supplies, and equipment (IRC §117(a), (b)). Klein's $12,000 scholarship was used for tuition and fees and was not a payment for services, so it is fully excluded. The $5,000 Klein earned for teaching courses at another college is compensation for services and is included in gross income (IRC §61(a)(1)).

Included: $5,000 teaching compensation
Excluded: $12,000 scholarship used for tuition and fees

The $17,000 amount wrongly adds the excluded scholarship. The $12,000 amount includes the scholarship and leaves out the wages, and $0 overlooks that the teaching pay is ordinary compensation.
questions.explanationJa:
学位取得を目指す学生が受け取る適格奨学金は、授業料・必須の諸費用・書籍・用品に充てた部分が非課税です（IRC §117(a)(b)）。Klein の奨学金$12,000は授業料等に充てられ、役務の対価でもないので全額非課税です。一方、別の大学で教えて得た$5,000は役務の対価として総所得に含まれます（IRC §61(a)(1)）。

算入: 講義の報酬 $5,000　除外: 奨学金 $12,000

$17,000 は非課税の奨学金を足している点が誤りです。$12,000 は奨学金を含めて報酬を落としており、$0 は講義の報酬が通常の給与所得であることを見落としています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.15

questions.stem: Darr, an employee of Sorce C corporation, is not a shareholder. Which of the following would be included in a taxpayer's gross income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Employer-provided medical insurance coverage under a health plan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An $11,000 gift from the taxpayer's grandparents.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fair market value of land that the taxpayer inherited from an uncle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The dividend income on shares of stock that the taxpayer received for services rendered.

questions.explanation:
Dividends are specifically included in gross income (IRC §61(a)(7)). It does not matter that the shares were originally received as compensation for services; the stock's value was income when received (IRC §83), and dividends later paid on the stock are dividend income.

Employer-provided medical insurance coverage under a health plan is excluded from the employee's income (IRC §106(a)). The $11,000 gift from grandparents is excluded from the recipient's income (IRC §102(a)); any gift tax consequences fall on the donor. The fair market value of land inherited from an uncle is excluded as property acquired by inheritance (IRC §102(a)).
questions.explanationJa:
配当は総所得に含まれます（IRC §61(a)(7)）。株式を役務の対価として受け取ったかどうかは関係なく、株式の時価は受取時に所得となり（IRC §83）、その後に支払われる配当は配当所得です。

雇用主が負担する健康保険は従業員の所得から除外されます（IRC §106(a)）。祖父母からの$11,000の贈与は受贈者の所得に含まれません（IRC §102(a)。贈与税は贈与者側の問題）。叔父から相続した土地の時価も相続財産として非課税です（IRC §102(a)）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.16

questions.stem:
Harold sustained a serious injury in the course of his employment. As a result of this injury, Harold received the following payments during the current year:

Payment | Amount
Workers' compensation | $6,500
Employer plan reimbursement of medical costs* | 4,000
Damages for personal physical injuries | 16,000

* Reimbursement from his employer's insurance plan for medical expenses paid by Harold and not deducted by him.

The amount to be included in Harold's gross income for the current year should be
questions.explanation:
Each payment is excluded from gross income:

Workers' compensation for an occupational injury is excluded (IRC §104(a)(1)).
Reimbursement from an employer-provided accident or health plan for medical care expenses is excluded (IRC §105(b)); because Harold did not deduct the medical expenses, there is no tax benefit to recapture.
Damages received on account of personal physical injuries are excluded (IRC §104(a)(2)).

Included in gross income: $0 + $0 + $0 = $0

The $26,500 amount wrongly includes all three payments. The $16,000 amount wrongly includes the physical injury damages, and the $4,000 amount wrongly includes the medical reimbursement, which would be taxable only to the extent the expenses had been deducted in a prior year.
questions.explanationJa:
3つの受取額はいずれも総所得から除外されます。

業務上の負傷による労災補償は非課税です（IRC §104(a)(1)）。
雇用主の健康保険制度からの医療費の払戻しは非課税です（IRC §105(b)）。Harold は医療費を控除していないので、過去の控除を取り戻す必要もありません。
身体的傷害に基づく損害賠償金は非課税です（IRC §104(a)(2)）。

算入額は $0 です。

$26,500 は3つすべてを含めており誤りです。$16,000 は身体的傷害の賠償金を、$4,000 は医療費の払戻しを含めている点が誤りです（払戻しは前年以前に医療費控除を受けていた場合にだけ課税されます）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.17

questions.stem: Walt's employer pays 100% of the cost of all employees' group term life insurance under a qualified plan. Under this plan, the maximum amount of tax-free coverage that may be provided for Walt by his employer is
questions.explanation:
IRC §79(a) excludes from an employee's gross income the cost of employer-provided group term life insurance on the employee's life up to $50,000 of coverage. The cost of coverage above $50,000 (computed using the IRS Uniform Premium Table, Treas. Reg. §1.79-3) is included in the employee's income, reduced by any amount the employee paid.

The $100,000 amount exceeds the statutory limit. The $10,000 and $5,000 amounts understate it; $5,000 is a different figure that relates to the old employee death benefit exclusion, which has been repealed.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §79(a) により、雇用主が負担する団体定期生命保険は保険金額$50,000までの保険料相当額が従業員の所得から除外されます。$50,000を超える部分の保険料相当額（IRSの統一保険料表で計算、Treas. Reg. §1.79-3）は、従業員の負担額を差し引いて所得に含めます。

$100,000 は法定の上限を超えています。$10,000 と $5,000 は上限を過小にしています（$5,000 は廃止された従業員死亡給付金の非課税枠の金額です）。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.18

questions.stem: Don Wolf became a general partner in Gata Associates on January 1, Year 1, with a 5% interest in Gata's profits, losses, and capital. Gata is a distributor of auto parts. Wolf does not materially participate in the partnership business. For Year 1, Gata had an operating loss of $100,000. In addition, Gata earned interest of $20,000 on a temporary investment. Gata has kept the principal temporarily invested while awaiting delivery of equipment that is presently on order. The principal will be used to pay for this equipment. Wolf's passive loss for Year 1 is
questions.explanation:
A trade or business in which the taxpayer does not materially participate is a passive activity (IRC §469(c)(1)). Wolf does not materially participate in Gata's auto parts business, so his share of the operating loss is a passive loss. Interest earned on funds set aside for working capital or future business needs is portfolio income, not passive income, even when the funds will be used in the business (IRC §469(e)(1); Treas. Reg. §1.469-2T(c)(3)). Portfolio income cannot be netted against the passive loss.

Passive loss: $100,000 x 5% = $5,000
Portfolio interest income (separately reported): $20,000 x 5% = $1,000

The $4,000 amount incorrectly nets the $1,000 share of portfolio interest against the passive loss. The $6,000 amount incorrectly adds the interest to the loss, and $0 ignores that a non-materially participating general partner's share of the business loss is passive.
questions.explanationJa:
納税者が実質的に関与しない事業は passive activity（受動的活動）です（IRC §469(c)(1)）。Wolf は Gata の事業に実質的に関与していないので、営業損失の持分は受動的損失です。運転資金や将来の設備購入に充てるため一時的に運用した資金の利息は、事業で使う予定であっても portfolio income（ポートフォリオ所得）で、受動的所得ではありません（IRC §469(e)(1)、Treas. Reg. §1.469-2T(c)(3)）。受動的損失と相殺できません。

受動的損失: $100,000 × 5% ＝ $5,000
ポートフォリオ所得（別建て）: $20,000 × 5% ＝ $1,000

$4,000 は利息$1,000を受動的損失と相殺しており誤りです。$6,000 は利息を損失に足しており、$0 は実質的に関与しないゼネラル・パートナーの事業損失が受動的損失になることを無視しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.20

questions.stem:
Mock operates a retail business selling illegal narcotic substances. Which of the following item(s) may Mock deduct in calculating business income?
I. Cost of merchandise
II. Business expenses other than the cost of merchandise

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
IRC §280E disallows any deduction or credit for amounts paid or incurred in carrying on a trade or business that consists of trafficking in controlled substances. However, cost of goods sold is not a deduction; it is a reduction of gross receipts in arriving at gross income (Treas. Reg. §1.61-3(a)). Because §280E reaches only deductions and credits, Mock may still subtract the cost of merchandise, but may not deduct other business expenses such as rent, wages, or advertising.

II only and Both I and II are incorrect because §280E bars the other business expenses. Neither I nor II is incorrect because the cost of merchandise is recovered through cost of goods sold, which §280E does not disallow.
questions.explanationJa:
IRC §280E は、規制薬物の売買を営む事業で支出した金額について、あらゆる控除と税額控除を認めません。ただし売上原価は「控除」ではなく、総収入から差し引いて総所得を求める要素です（Treas. Reg. §1.61-3(a)）。§280E が否認するのは控除と税額控除だけなので、商品の原価は差し引けますが、家賃・給与・広告費などの他の事業経費は控除できません。

II only と Both I and II は、§280E が他の事業経費を否認する点で誤りです。Neither I nor II は、商品の原価が売上原価として回収でき §280E の対象外である点で誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.21

questions.stem: Adam Jackson owns a second residence that is used for both personal and rental purposes. During Year 1, Jackson used the second residence for 50 days and rented the residence for 200 days. Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Depreciation may not be deducted on the property under any circumstances.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A rental loss may be deducted if rental-related expenses exceed rental income.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Utilities and maintenance on the property must be divided between personal and rental use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All mortgage interest and taxes on the property will be deducted to determine the property's net income or loss.

questions.explanation:
A dwelling unit is treated as used as a residence if personal use exceeds the greater of 14 days or 10% of the days rented at fair rental (IRC §280A(d)(1)). Jackson's 50 personal days exceed the greater of 14 days or 20 days (10% x 200), so the vacation home rules apply. Expenses must be allocated between rental and personal use based on days of use (IRC §280A(e)), so utilities and maintenance are divided between the two uses. Rental deductions are then limited to rental income (IRC §280A(c)(5)).

The statement that depreciation may not be deducted under any circumstances is incorrect; depreciation on the rental portion is allowed to the extent of remaining rental income. The statement that a rental loss may be deducted is incorrect because §280A(c)(5) does not allow a loss when the property is used as a residence. The statement that all mortgage interest and taxes are deducted in computing rental net income is incorrect; only the rental portion is used against rental income, and the personal portion is treated as a personal (itemized) item.
questions.explanationJa:
私的使用日数が「14日」と「公正な賃料で貸した日数の10%」の多い方を超えると、その住宅は住居として扱われます（IRC §280A(d)(1)）。Jackson の私的使用50日は、14日と20日（200日×10%）の多い方を超えるので、別荘の規定が適用されます。経費は使用日数で賃貸用と私的用に按分しなければならず（IRC §280A(e)）、光熱費や維持費も按分します。さらに賃貸の経費控除は賃貸収入が上限です（IRC §280A(c)(5)）。

「減価償却はどんな場合も控除できない」は誤りで、賃貸部分の減価償却は残りの賃貸収入の範囲で控除できます。「賃貸損失を控除できる」は、住居扱いの場合 §280A(c)(5) で損失が認められないので誤りです。「住宅ローン利息と税金の全額を賃貸の純損益計算で差し引く」も誤りで、賃貸収入から差し引けるのは賃貸部分だけ、私的部分は個人の項目（項目別控除）として扱います。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.22

questions.stem: In the current year, Jane won $6,000 in a state lottery. Jane also spent $300 for the purchase of lottery tickets. Jane elected the standard deduction on her current year income tax return. The amount of lottery winnings that should be included in Jane's current year taxable income is
questions.explanation:
Gambling and lottery winnings are included in gross income in full (IRC §61(a)). Wagering losses, including the cost of losing lottery tickets, are deductible only as an itemized deduction and only to the extent of wagering gains (IRC §165(d); IRC §67(b)(3)); for tax years beginning after 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act further limits the deduction to 90% of wagering losses. Because Jane elected the standard deduction, she gets no deduction for the $300 of ticket costs, and the entire $6,000 of winnings remains in taxable income.

The $5,700 amount ($6,000 - $300) would be reached only by a taxpayer who itemizes; it wrongly nets the ticket cost against the winnings. The $0 and $2,000 amounts have no basis, since lottery winnings are fully taxable and there is no exclusion for them.
questions.explanationJa:
宝くじ・ギャンブルの当選金は全額が総所得に含まれます（IRC §61(a)）。外れ券の購入費などの賭博損失は、項目別控除としてのみ、かつ賭博利得の範囲でしか控除できません（IRC §165(d)、§67(b)(3)。2026年以降はOBBBAにより控除できる損失が賭博損失の90%に制限）。Jane は標準控除を選んでいるので$300は控除できず、当選金$6,000がそのまま課税所得に入ります。

$5,700（$6,000－$300）は項目別控除を選んだ場合の考え方で、当選金と購入費を相殺している点が誤りです。$0 や $2,000 は、宝くじの当選金に非課税枠が無いことから根拠がありません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.24

questions.stem:
Kent received the following interest income:

Source of interest | Amount
On VA insurance dividends on deposit with VA* | $20
On U.S. Treasury certificates | 30
On state income tax refund | 40

* Veterans Administration insurance dividends left on deposit with the VA.

What amount should Kent include for interest income in his tax return?
questions.explanation:
Interest on Veterans Administration (VA) insurance dividends left on deposit with the VA is not taxable; veterans' benefits, including these dividends and the interest on them, are exempt (38 U.S.C. §5301(a)). Interest on U.S. Treasury obligations is fully taxable for federal purposes (IRC §61(a)(4)); it is exempt only from state income tax. Interest paid on a state income tax refund is also taxable interest income (IRC §61(a)(4)).

Treasury certificates: $30
State income tax refund interest: $40
Taxable interest: $30 + $40 = $70

The $90 amount wrongly includes the $20 of VA dividend interest. The $50 amount ($20 + $30) includes the exempt VA interest and omits the interest on the tax refund, and the $20 amount includes only the exempt VA interest.
questions.explanationJa:
退役軍人局（VA）の保険配当をVAに預けたままにして生じる利息は非課税です（退役軍人給付として 38 U.S.C. §5301(a) で非課税）。米国財務省証券の利息は連邦税では全額課税で、州所得税だけが非課税です（IRC §61(a)(4)）。州所得税の還付金に付く利息も課税される利子所得です。

財務省証券 $30 ＋ 州税還付の利息 $40 ＝ $70

$90 は非課税のVA配当の利息$20を含めている点が誤りです。$50（$20＋$30）は非課税の利息を含め還付利息を落としており、$20 は非課税の利息だけを計上しています。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.25

questions.stem:
Baum, an unmarried optometrist and sole proprietor of Optics, buys and maintains a supply of eyeglasses and frames to sell in the ordinary course of business. In Year 1, Optics had $350,000 in gross business receipts and its year-end inventory was not subject to the uniform capitalization rules. Baum's Year 1 adjusted gross income was $90,000 and Baum qualified to itemize deductions. During Year 1, Baum recorded the following information:

Business expenses | Amount
Optics cost of goods sold | $35,000
Optics rent expense | 28,000
Liability insurance premium on Optics | 5,250

Other expenditures | Amount
Baum's self-employment tax | $29,750
Baum's self-employment health insurance | 8,750
Estimated Year 1 federal income tax payments | 13,500

What amount should Baum report as Year 1 net earnings from self-employment?
questions.explanation:
Net earnings from self-employment start from the gross income derived from the trade or business less the deductions attributable to that business (IRC §1402(a)). Only the Optics business items are subtracted:

Gross business receipts: $350,000
Less cost of goods sold: $35,000
Less rent expense: $28,000
Less liability insurance premium: $5,250
Net earnings from self-employment: $350,000 - $35,000 - $28,000 - $5,250 = $281,750

Self-employment tax, self-employed health insurance, and estimated income tax payments are personal items, not expenses of the business. The deduction for one half of self-employment tax and the self-employed health insurance deduction are adjustments to arrive at AGI and do not reduce net earnings from self-employment (IRC §164(f); IRC §162(l)(4)). The 92.35% adjustment of §1402(a)(12) is applied afterward on Schedule SE when computing the tax.

The $252,000 amount wrongly subtracts the $29,750 of self-employment tax, the $273,000 amount wrongly subtracts the $8,750 of health insurance, and the $243,250 amount wrongly subtracts both.
questions.explanationJa:
自営業による純所得（net earnings from self-employment）は、事業の総収入から、その事業に係る経費を差し引いて求めます（IRC §1402(a)）。差し引くのは Optics の事業経費だけです。

$350,000 －売上原価 $35,000 －家賃 $28,000 －賠償責任保険料 $5,250 ＝ $281,750

自営業税・自営業者の健康保険料・所得税の予定納税は個人の支出で、事業経費ではありません。自営業税の1/2控除と自営業者の健康保険料控除はAGIを求める際の調整項目で、自営業の純所得は減らしません（IRC §164(f)、§162(l)(4)）。§1402(a)(12) の92.35%の調整は、その後 Schedule SE で税額を計算する段階で行います。

$252,000 は自営業税$29,750を、$273,000 は健康保険料$8,750を、$243,250 はその両方を差し引いている点が誤りです。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.26

questions.stem:
Destry, a single taxpayer, reported the following on his U.S. Individual Income Tax Return Form 1040:

Item | Amount
Income: Wages | $5,000
Income: Interest on savings account | 1,000
Income: Net rental income | 4,000
Deductions: Personal exemption | 3,650
Deductions: Standard deduction | 5,700
Deductions: Net business loss | 20,000
Deductions: Net short-term capital loss | 2,000

What is Destry's net operating loss that is available for carryback or carryforward?
questions.explanation:
An individual's net operating loss is computed under IRC §172(d) with these modifications: no deduction for personal exemptions (§172(d)(3)); nonbusiness capital losses are allowed only to the extent of nonbusiness capital gains (§172(d)(2)); and nonbusiness deductions (including the standard deduction) are allowed only to the extent of nonbusiness income (§172(d)(4)). Wages and net rental income are treated as business income; interest on savings is nonbusiness income.
Total income = $5,000 + $1,000 + $4,000 = $10,000
Less net business loss = $10,000 - $20,000 = -$10,000
Standard deduction allowed only up to nonbusiness interest income of $1,000 = -$10,000 - $1,000 = -$11,000
Personal exemption: not allowed; short-term capital loss: not allowed (no nonbusiness capital gains)
NOL = $11,000 (equivalently, $20,000 business loss - $5,000 wages - $4,000 rental income).
Under current law the personal exemption amount is zero in any event, and an individual's NOL arising after 2020 is carried forward indefinitely (no carryback, except farming losses) and may offset only 80% of taxable income in the carryforward year; the amount of the NOL itself is still $11,000.
The $13,000 amount incorrectly includes the $2,000 short-term capital loss. The $20,000 amount is the business loss before offsetting the wages and rental income. The $20,350 amount incorrectly deducts the full standard deduction and personal exemption against the income.
questions.explanationJa:
個人のNOLは§172(d)の修正を加えて計算する。人的控除は認められず、非事業のキャピタル・ロスは非事業のキャピタル・ゲインの範囲でしか認められず、非事業の控除（標準控除を含む）は非事業の所得の範囲でしか認められない。給与と純賃貸所得は事業所得、預金利息は非事業所得として扱う。
所得合計 $5,000 + $1,000 + $4,000 = $10,000
事業損失を控除: $10,000 − $20,000 = −$10,000
標準控除は非事業所得の利息$1,000まで: −$10,000 − $1,000 = −$11,000
人的控除と短期キャピタル・ロス$2,000は加算しない
NOLは$11,000（事業損失$20,000 − 給与$5,000 − 賃貸所得$4,000と同じ）。
現行法では人的控除額はそもそもゼロで、2021年以降に生じた個人のNOLは繰戻しができず（農業損失を除く）無期限に繰り越し、繰越年度の課税所得の80%までしか控除できないが、NOLの金額自体は$11,000で変わらない。
$13,000は短期キャピタル・ロス$2,000を含めた誤り、$20,000は給与・賃貸所得と相殺する前の事業損失、$20,350は標準控除と人的控除を全額差し引いた誤り。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.28

questions.stem: Dale received $1,000 in the current year for jury duty. In exchange for regular compensation from her employer during the period of jury service, Dale was required to remit the entire $1,000 to her employer. In Dale's income tax return, the $1,000 jury duty fee should be

choices.label: A
choices.text: Claimed in full as an itemized deduction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Claimed as an itemized deduction to the extent exceeding 2% of adjusted gross income

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deducted from gross income in arriving at adjusted gross income

choices.label: D
choices.text: Included in taxable income without a corresponding offset against other income

questions.explanation:
Jury duty pay is included in gross income, but IRC §62(a)(13) allows an above-the-line deduction (in arriving at adjusted gross income) for jury duty pay that the taxpayer is required to remit to the employer in exchange for regular compensation during the jury service. Dale therefore includes the $1,000 in gross income and deducts the same $1,000 in arriving at AGI, so the net effect is zero.
Claiming the amount in full as an itemized deduction is wrong because the deduction is for AGI, not from AGI. Claiming it as an itemized deduction subject to the 2% of AGI floor is wrong for the same reason, and miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to the 2% floor are no longer allowed under current law. Including it in taxable income without a corresponding offset ignores the §62(a)(13) deduction.
questions.explanationJa:
陪審員手当は総所得に含まれるが、雇用主から通常の給与を受け取る代わりに手当を雇用主へ渡すことが求められている場合、渡した額は§62(a)(13)によりAGIの計算上（for AGI）控除できる。Daleは$1,000を総所得に含め、同じ$1,000をAGI算定前に控除するので、差し引きゼロになる。
全額を項目別控除とするのは、AGI前の控除であるため誤り。AGIの2%を超える部分を項目別控除とするのも同じ理由で誤りで、2%フロアの雑項目控除は現行法ではそもそも認められない。相殺なしで課税所得に含めるのは§62(a)(13)の控除を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.29

questions.stem: For calendar Year 1, Ralph earned $1,000 interest at Ridge Savings Bank on a certificate of deposit scheduled to mature in Year 3. In January Year 2, before filing his Year 1 income tax return, Ralph incurred a forfeiture penalty of $500 for premature withdrawal of the funds. Ralph should treat this $500 forfeiture penalty as a

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduction of interest earned in Year 1, so that only $500 of such interest is taxable on Ralph's Year 1 return

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deduction from Year 2 adjusted gross income, deductible only if Ralph itemizes his deductions for Year 2

choices.label: C
choices.text: Penalty not deductible for tax purposes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deduction from gross income in arriving at Year 2 adjusted gross income

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §62(a)(9), a penalty paid to a bank for premature withdrawal of funds from a time savings account or certificate of deposit is deductible in arriving at adjusted gross income. The deduction is taken in the year the penalty is incurred (Year 2). The $1,000 of interest earned in Year 1 remains fully taxable in Year 1.
Reducing the Year 1 interest so that only $500 is taxable is wrong because the penalty was not incurred until Year 2 and does not reduce the interest already earned. Treating it as an itemized deduction available only if Ralph itemizes is wrong because it is an above-the-line deduction. Treating the penalty as nondeductible ignores §62(a)(9).
questions.explanationJa:
定期預金を満期前に引き出したことによる違約金は、§62(a)(9)によりAGIの計算上（for AGI）控除できる。控除するのは違約金が発生した年（Year 2）。Year 1に稼得した利息$1,000はYear 1にすべて課税される。
Year 1の利息を減らして$500だけ課税とするのは、違約金がYear 2に発生したもので既に稼得した利息を減らさないため誤り。項目別控除を選んだ場合だけ控除できるとするのは、AGI前の控除であるため誤り。控除不可とするのは§62(a)(9)を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.31

questions.stem: Val and Pat White, both age 45, filed a joint return for 2012. Val earned $36,000 in wages and was covered by his employer's qualified pension plan. Pat was unemployed and received $4,000 in alimony payments for the first 4 months of the year before remarrying. The couple had no other income. Each contributed $5,000 to an IRA account. The allowable IRA deduction on their joint 2012 tax return is
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §219, each spouse may deduct traditional IRA contributions up to the annual limit (the 2012 limit was $5,000 per person). On a joint return, the spousal IRA rule of §219(c) lets a spouse with little or no compensation contribute based on the couple's combined compensation, so Val's $36,000 of wages supports both $5,000 contributions.
Val is an active participant in an employer plan, so his deduction is subject to the §219(g) phase-out, but the couple's modified AGI ($36,000 wages + $4,000 alimony = $40,000) is far below the phase-out range for joint filers. Pat is not an active participant, and the phase-out for a spouse of an active participant also starts at a much higher AGI.
Deduction = $5,000 (Val) + $5,000 (Pat) = $10,000.
Under current law the annual limit is higher ($7,500 for 2026) and the phase-out ranges are higher, so the same facts would still give a $10,000 deduction.
The $9,000 amount incorrectly limits Pat's deduction to her $4,000 of alimony; the spousal IRA rule uses the couple's combined compensation. The $5,000 amount allows a deduction for only one spouse. The $0 amount wrongly assumes Val's plan coverage eliminates the deduction at this AGI level.
questions.explanationJa:
§219により、各配偶者は年間限度額（2012年は1人$5,000）までIRA拠出を控除できる。合算申告では§219(c)の配偶者IRAの規定により、所得の少ない配偶者も夫婦合算の報酬をもとに拠出でき、Valの給与$36,000で2人分$5,000ずつの拠出を賄える。
Valは企業年金の加入者なので§219(g)の段階的縮小の対象になるが、夫婦の修正AGIは給与$36,000＋扶養料$4,000＝$40,000で、合算申告の縮小範囲を大きく下回る。Patは加入者ではなく、加入者の配偶者に対する縮小もはるかに高いAGIから始まる。
控除額 $5,000（Val）＋$5,000（Pat）＝$10,000。
現行法では年間限度額（2026年は$7,500）も縮小範囲も引き上げられており、同じ事実なら控除額はやはり$10,000になる。
$9,000はPatの控除を扶養料の$4,000に限った誤りで、配偶者IRAは合算報酬で判定する。$5,000は一方の配偶者しか控除していない。$0はValが年金加入者であることだけで控除がなくなるとした誤り。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.35

questions.stem: Davis, a sole proprietor with no employees, has a Keogh profit-sharing plan to which he may contribute 20% of his annual earned income. For this purpose, "earned income" is defined as net self-employment earnings reduced by the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deductible Keogh contribution

choices.label: B
choices.text: Self-employment tax

choices.label: C
choices.text: Self-employment tax and one-half of the deductible Keogh contribution

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deductible Keogh contribution and one-half of the self-employment tax

questions.explanation:
For a self-employed individual, "earned income" for a Keogh (H.R. 10) plan is net earnings from self-employment reduced by the deduction for one-half of self-employment tax (IRC §164(f)) and by the deductible contribution to the plan itself (IRC §401(c)(2)). Because the contribution reduces the base on which it is computed, a 25% plan rate is effectively 20% of net earnings after the one-half SE tax deduction.
Reducing earnings by the deductible Keogh contribution alone omits the one-half SE tax deduction. Reducing by the full self-employment tax overstates the reduction, since only one-half of SE tax is deductible. Reducing by the full SE tax and one-half of the Keogh contribution reverses the two items.
questions.explanationJa:
自営業者のKeogh（H.R. 10）プランにおける「earned income」は、自営業純所得から、自営業税の2分の1の控除（§164(f)）と、プランへの控除対象拠出額そのもの（§401(c)(2)）を差し引いた額である。拠出額が自らの計算基礎を減らすため、プラン上25%の率は自営業税半額控除後の純所得の実質20%になる。
Keogh拠出額だけを差し引くのは自営業税半額の控除を落としている。自営業税の全額を差し引くのは、控除できるのが半額だけなので過大。自営業税の全額とKeogh拠出額の半額を差し引くのは、2つの項目を取り違えている。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.36

questions.stem:
Which of the following requirements must be met in order for a single individual to qualify for the additional standard deduction amount?
Must be age 65 or older or blind | Must support dependent child or aged parent

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: B
choices.text: No | No

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes | No

choices.label: D
choices.text: No | Yes

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §63(f), the additional standard deduction is available to a taxpayer who is age 65 or older or blind (an additional amount for each condition). There is no requirement that the taxpayer support a dependent child or an aged parent; supporting a qualifying person is relevant to head of household filing status, not to the additional standard deduction.
Requiring both age/blindness and support of a dependent adds a condition that does not exist. Requiring neither ignores the age-65-or-blind test. Requiring only support of a dependent confuses the additional standard deduction with head of household status.
questions.explanationJa:
§63(f)により、追加の標準控除は65歳以上または視覚障害者である納税者に認められる（該当する条件ごとに加算）。扶養する子や高齢の親を支えている必要はない。扶養者を支えることは世帯主（head of household）の申告資格の要件であり、追加の標準控除の要件ではない。
両方を要件とするのは存在しない条件を加えている。どちらも不要とするのは65歳以上・視覚障害の要件を無視している。扶養のみを要件とするのは世帯主の申告資格と混同している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.37

questions.stem:
In the current year, Drake, a disabled taxpayer, made the following home improvements:

Improvement | Cost
Pool installation (see note 1) | $100,000
Widening doorways for wheelchair (see note 2) | 10,000

Note 1: The pool installation qualified as a medical expense and increased the value of the home by $25,000.
Note 2: Widening doorways to accommodate Drake's wheelchair did not increase the value of his home.

For regular income tax purposes and without regard to the adjusted gross income percentage threshold limitation, what maximum amount would be allowable as a medical expense deduction in the current year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §213 and Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(e)(1)(iii), a capital expenditure for a home improvement made primarily for medical care is deductible as a medical expense only to the extent the cost exceeds the increase in the value of the property. Improvements made to accommodate a disabled person's residence, such as widening doorways, generally do not increase value and are fully deductible.
Pool: $100,000 - $25,000 increase in value = $75,000
Widening doorways: $10,000 (no increase in value)
Total medical expense = $75,000 + $10,000 = $85,000
The $110,000 amount ignores the $25,000 increase in home value from the pool. The $75,000 amount omits the doorway widening. The $10,000 amount omits the deductible portion of the pool.
questions.explanationJa:
§213とTreas. Reg. §1.213-1(e)(1)(iii)により、主として医療目的で行う住宅の資本的支出は、費用のうち資産価値の増加額を超える部分だけが医療費控除の対象になる。障害者の住居に合わせる改修（出入口の拡幅など）は通常価値を増やさないので全額が対象。
プール: $100,000 − 価値増加$25,000 = $75,000
出入口の拡幅: $10,000（価値増加なし）
医療費合計 $75,000 + $10,000 = $85,000
$110,000はプールによる価値増加$25,000を差し引いていない。$75,000は出入口の拡幅を落としている。$10,000はプールの控除対象部分を落としている。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.39

questions.stem:
Tom and Sally White, married and both 40 years old, derive their entire income from the operation of their retail stationery shop.
