Their adjusted gross income on their joint income tax return was $100,000. The Whites itemized their deductions on Schedule A. The following unreimbursed cash expenditures were among those made by the Whites during the current year:

Expenditure | Amount
Wheelchair repair (note 1) | $600
Special school for handicapped child (note 2) | 8,000

Note 1: Repair and maintenance of motorized wheelchair for physically handicapped dependent child.
Note 2: Tuition, meals, and lodging at special school for physically handicapped dependent child in an institution primarily for the availability of medical care, with meals and lodging furnished as necessary incidents to that care.

Without regard to the adjusted gross income percentage threshold, what amount may the Whites claim as qualifying medical expenses?
questions.explanation:
Medical care under IRC §213(d) includes amounts paid for the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease and for the purpose of affecting any structure or function of the body. Repair and maintenance of a motorized wheelchair for a dependent is a medical expense. Under Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(e)(1)(v), when an individual is in an institution (including a special school) primarily for the availability of medical care, the entire cost, including tuition, meals, and lodging furnished as a necessary incident to that care, is a medical expense.
Qualifying medical expenses = $600 + $8,000 = $8,600
The $8,000 amount omits the wheelchair repair. The $600 amount omits the special school costs, which qualify because the child attends primarily for medical care. The $0 amount treats both items as personal expenses.
questions.explanationJa:
§213(d)の医療には、疾病の診断・治療・予防や身体の構造・機能への作用を目的とする支出が含まれる。扶養する子の電動車いすの修理・維持費は医療費。Treas. Reg. §1.213-1(e)(1)(v)により、主として医療を受けるために施設（特別支援学校を含む）にいる場合、授業料や医療に必然的に伴う食事・宿泊費も含め全額が医療費になる。
医療費 $600 + $8,000 = $8,600
$8,000は車いすの修理を落としている。$600は特別支援学校の費用を落としているが、子は主として医療のために在籍しているので対象になる。$0は両方を個人的支出とした誤り。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.40

questions.stem:
Carroll is 35 years old and an unmarried taxpayer with an adjusted gross income of $100,000. Carroll incurred and paid the following unreimbursed medical expenses for the year:

Expense | Amount
Doctor bills resulting from a serious fall | $5,000
Cosmetic surgery (congenital deformity) | 15,000

Carroll had no medical insurance. For regular income tax purposes, what was Carroll's maximum allowable medical expense deduction, after the applicable threshold limitation, for the year?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §213(d)(9), cosmetic surgery is generally not medical care, but surgery necessary to ameliorate a deformity arising from a congenital abnormality, a personal injury from accident or trauma, or a disfiguring disease is deductible. Both expenses therefore qualify. Medical expenses are deductible only to the extent they exceed 7.5% of AGI (§213(a)).
Qualifying expenses = $5,000 + $15,000 = $20,000
Threshold = $100,000 x 7.5% = $7,500
Deduction = $20,000 - $7,500 = $12,500
The $0 amount treats the cosmetic surgery as nondeductible and then finds the $5,000 doctor bills below the floor. The $15,000 amount deducts only the surgery cost without the floor. The $20,000 amount ignores the 7.5% of AGI floor.
questions.explanationJa:
§213(d)(9)により美容整形は原則として医療費にならないが、先天的な異常による変形を改善するために必要な手術は医療費になる。したがって2つの支出はどちらも対象。医療費はAGIの7.5%を超える部分だけ控除できる（§213(a)）。
対象医療費 $5,000 + $15,000 = $20,000
足切り額 $100,000 × 7.5% = $7,500
控除額 $20,000 − $7,500 = $12,500
$0は手術を控除不可とし、医師の費用$5,000が足切り額未満になるとした誤り。$15,000は手術費だけを足切りなしで控除している。$20,000はAGIの7.5%の足切りを無視している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.41

questions.stem: An individual starts paying student loan interest in the current year. How many years may the individual deduct a portion of the student loan interest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Current year only

choices.label: B
choices.text: Five years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ten years

choices.label: D
choices.text: Duration of time that interest is paid

questions.explanation:
IRC §221 allows an above-the-line deduction of up to $2,500 per year for interest paid on a qualified education loan, subject to an income phase-out. The former rule limiting the deduction to the first 60 months of required payments was repealed, so the deduction is available for as long as qualifying interest is paid.
Limiting the deduction to the current year only has no basis in §221. A five-year limit reflects the repealed 60-month rule. A ten-year period is not a limit found anywhere in §221.
questions.explanationJa:
§221により、適格な教育ローンの利息は年$2,500を上限に（所得による段階的縮小あり）AGI前に控除できる。以前の「返済開始から60か月まで」の制限は廃止されたので、適格な利息を支払う限り控除できる。
当年のみとする根拠は§221に無い。5年は廃止された60か月ルールに基づく誤り。10年という制限も§221には無い。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.42

questions.stem:
Jackson owns two residences. The second residence, which has never been used for rental purposes, is the only residence that is subject to a mortgage. The following expenses were incurred for the second residence:

Expense | Amount
Mortgage interest | $5,000
Utilities | 1,200
Insurance | 6,000

For regular income tax purposes, what is the maximum amount allowable as a deduction for Jackson's second residence?

choices.label: A
choices.text: $6,200 in determining adjusted gross income

choices.label: B
choices.text: $11,000 in determining adjusted gross income

choices.label: C
choices.text: $5,000 as an itemized deduction

choices.label: D
choices.text: $12,200 as an itemized deduction

questions.explanation:
Qualified residence interest is deductible as an itemized deduction under IRC §163(h)(3). A qualified residence includes the principal residence and one other residence selected by the taxpayer (§163(h)(4)), so mortgage interest on Jackson's second home is deductible. Utilities and insurance on a personal-use residence that is never rented are nondeductible personal expenses (§262).
Deduction = mortgage interest $5,000 as an itemized deduction
The $6,200 in determining AGI treats nondeductible utilities and insurance as deductible and places them above the line. The $11,000 in determining AGI adds insurance to the interest and treats it as a deduction for AGI. The $12,200 itemized deduction includes the nondeductible utilities and insurance.
questions.explanationJa:
適格住宅利息は§163(h)(3)により項目別控除できる。適格住宅には主たる住居と納税者が選ぶもう1つの住居が含まれる（§163(h)(4)）ので、Jacksonの別宅の住宅ローン利息は控除できる。一度も賃貸していない個人用住居の光熱費と保険料は個人的支出で控除できない（§262）。
控除額は住宅ローン利息$5,000（項目別控除）
AGI計算上$6,200は控除できない光熱費と保険料をAGI前に控除している。AGI計算上$11,000は保険料を利息に加え、AGI前の控除としている。項目別控除$12,200は控除できない光熱費と保険料を含めている。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.43

questions.stem:
Wilson, CPA, uses a commercial tax software package to prepare clients' individual income tax returns. Upon reviewing a client's computer-generated year 1 itemized deductions, Wilson discovers that the schedule's deductible investment interest expense is less than the amount paid by the taxpayer and the amount that Wilson entered into the computer. After analyzing the entire tax return, Wilson determines that the computer-generated investment interest expense deduction is correct. Why is the computer-generated investment interest expense deduction correct?
I. The client's investment interest expense exceeds net investment income.
II. The client's qualified residence interest expense reduces the deductible amount of investment interest expense.

choices.label: A
choices.text: I only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both I and II

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither I nor II

questions.explanation:
Under IRC §163(d)(1), an individual's deduction for investment interest expense is limited to net investment income for the year; any excess is carried forward to future years (§163(d)(2)). If the client's investment interest exceeds net investment income, the software correctly deducts less than the amount paid. Qualified residence interest is a separate category of deductible interest under §163(h)(3) and does not reduce the investment interest deduction.
So statement I explains the result and statement II does not.
Selecting statement II alone, or both statements, wrongly treats qualified residence interest as reducing investment interest. Selecting neither statement ignores the net investment income limit.
questions.explanationJa:
§163(d)(1)により、個人の投資利息の控除は当年の純投資所得が上限で、超過分は翌年以降に繰り越す（§163(d)(2)）。投資利息が純投資所得を超えていれば、ソフトが支払額より少なく控除するのは正しい。適格住宅利息は§163(h)(3)による別枠の控除で、投資利息の控除を減らさない。
したがってIは理由になり、IIは理由にならない。
IIのみ、またはIとIIの両方とするのは、適格住宅利息が投資利息を減らすとした誤り。どちらでもないとするのは純投資所得の上限を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.44

questions.stem: An individual's losses on transactions entered into for personal purposes are deductible only if

choices.label: A
choices.text: The losses qualify as casualty or theft losses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The losses can be characterized as hobby losses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The losses do not exceed $3,000 ($6,000 on a joint return).

choices.label: D
choices.text: No part of the transactions was entered into for profit.

questions.explanation:
IRC §165(c) limits an individual's deductible losses to (1) losses incurred in a trade or business, (2) losses in transactions entered into for profit, and (3) casualty and theft losses of property not connected with a trade or business. A loss on a personal-purpose transaction (for example, selling a personal car or residence at a loss) is therefore deductible only if it is a casualty or theft loss. Under current law, a personal casualty or theft loss is further limited by §165(h)(5): it is deductible only if attributable to a federally declared disaster (and, beginning in 2026, certain state-declared disasters) or to the extent of personal casualty gains, so casualty or theft treatment is a necessary condition.
Hobby losses are not deductible at all against other income. The $3,000 ($6,000 on a joint return) amount is not a rule for personal losses; the capital loss limit is $3,000 for both single and joint returns, and it applies to investment capital losses, not personal-use losses. Requiring that no part of the transaction was for profit describes a personal transaction but does not make its loss deductible.
questions.explanationJa:
§165(c)により、個人が控除できる損失は(1)事業上の損失、(2)営利目的の取引の損失、(3)事業に関係しない資産の災害・盗難損失に限られる。個人目的の取引の損失（自家用車や自宅を損をして売った場合など）は、災害・盗難損失に当たる場合に限り控除できる。現行法では§165(h)(5)によりさらに限定され、個人の災害・盗難損失は連邦の災害指定地域の損失（2026年からは一定の州指定災害も含む）か個人の災害利得の範囲でしか控除できないので、災害・盗難損失であることは必要条件である。
趣味の損失は他の所得から控除できない。$3,000（合算$6,000）という規則は存在せず、キャピタル・ロスの控除限度は単身・合算とも$3,000で、個人使用資産の損失には適用されない。営利目的が一切ないことは個人取引の説明にすぎず、損失を控除可能にするものではない。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.45

questions.stem:
On January 2, Year 1, the Philips paid $50,000 cash and obtained a $200,000 mortgage to purchase a home. In Year 3, they borrowed $15,000 secured by their home, and used the cash to add a new room to their residence. That same year they took out a $5,000 auto loan. The following information pertains to interest paid in Year 7:

Interest | Amount
Mortgage interest | $17,000
Interest on room construction loan | 1,500
Auto loan interest | 500

For Year 7, how much interest is deductible, prior to any itemized deduction limitations?
questions.explanation:
Qualified residence interest is deductible under IRC §163(h)(3). Acquisition indebtedness is debt incurred to acquire, construct, or substantially improve a qualified residence and secured by it (§163(h)(3)). Under current law, interest on home equity debt is deductible only if the proceeds are used to buy, build, or substantially improve the home securing the loan. The $15,000 loan secured by the home and used to add a new room is therefore acquisition indebtedness. Total acquisition debt ($200,000 + $15,000 = $215,000) is well below the $750,000 limit. Interest on a personal auto loan is nondeductible personal interest (§163(h)(1)).
Deductible interest = $17,000 + $1,500 = $18,500
The $17,000 amount omits the room construction loan interest. The $17,500 amount adds the nondeductible auto loan interest instead of the construction loan interest. The $19,000 amount includes the nondeductible auto loan interest.
questions.explanationJa:
適格住宅利息は§163(h)(3)により控除できる。取得債務とは、適格住宅の取得・建築・大規模改良のために借り入れ、その住宅を担保とする債務（§163(h)(3)）。現行法では住宅を担保とする借入れの利息は、資金をその住宅の購入・建築・大規模改良に使った場合に限り控除できる。住宅を担保に借りて部屋の増築に使った$15,000は取得債務に当たる。取得債務の合計 $200,000 + $15,000 = $215,000 は上限$750,000を大きく下回る。自動車ローンの利息は個人的利息で控除できない（§163(h)(1)）。
控除できる利息 $17,000 + $1,500 = $18,500
$17,000は増築ローンの利息を落としている。$17,500は増築ローンの利息の代わりに控除できない自動車ローン利息を加えている。$19,000は控除できない自動車ローン利息を含めている。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.46

questions.stem: Wood's residence had an adjusted basis of $150,000 when it was destroyed by a tornado. An appraiser valued the decline in market value at $175,000. The tornado was not a federally declared disaster. Wood received $130,000 from his insurance company for the property loss and did not elect to deduct the casualty loss in an earlier year. Wood's adjusted gross income was $60,000 and he did not have any casualty gains. What total amount can Wood deduct as an itemized deduction for the casualty loss, after the application of the threshold limitations?
questions.explanation:
Under IRC §165(h)(5), a personal casualty loss of an individual is deductible only to the extent it is attributable to a federally declared disaster (and, beginning in 2026, certain state-declared disasters), except that personal casualty losses may still offset personal casualty gains. The tornado was not a federally declared disaster, the facts indicate no state disaster declaration, and Wood had no casualty gains, so none of the loss is deductible.
Even before the limitation, the measured loss would be: lesser of adjusted basis $150,000 or decline in value $175,000 = $150,000; less insurance $130,000 = $20,000; less $100 floor and 10% of AGI ($6,000). That loss is disallowed entirely under §165(h)(5).
Deduction = $0
The $39,000 and $38,900 amounts measure the loss using the $175,000 decline in value instead of the lower adjusted basis and also ignore the disaster requirement. The $19,900 amount applies only the $100 floor to the $20,000 net loss and ignores both the 10% of AGI floor and the federally declared disaster requirement.
questions.explanationJa:
§165(h)(5)により、個人の災害損失は連邦の災害指定地域に起因するもの（2026年からは一定の州指定災害も含む）に限り控除でき、例外は個人の災害利得との相殺だけである。竜巻は連邦の災害指定ではなく、州の災害指定があったという事実も示されておらず、Woodに災害利得もないので、損失は一切控除できない。
参考までに制限前の損失額は、取得価額$150,000と価値下落額$175,000の小さい方$150,000から保険金$130,000を引いた$20,000で、ここから$100とAGIの10%（$6,000）を差し引く計算になるが、§165(h)(5)により全額が否認される。
控除額 $0
$39,000と$38,900は取得価額より大きい価値下落額$175,000で損失を測っており、災害指定の要件も無視している。$19,900は損失$20,000から$100だけを引き、AGIの10%の足切りと災害指定の要件の両方を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.47

questions.stem: How may taxes paid by an individual to a foreign country be treated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: As an itemized deduction subject to the 2% floor

choices.label: B
choices.text: As a credit against federal income taxes due

choices.label: C
choices.text: As an adjustment to gross income

choices.label: D
choices.text: As nondeductible

questions.explanation:
An individual who pays income taxes to a foreign country may elect to claim them as a foreign tax credit against U.S. federal income tax (IRC §901, subject to the §904 limitation), or alternatively deduct them as an itemized deduction for taxes (§164(a)(3)). Among the stated treatments, the credit against federal income taxes is correct.
Treating foreign taxes as an itemized deduction subject to the 2% floor is wrong because taxes were never a 2% miscellaneous itemized deduction, and the 2% category is no longer allowed. Treating them as an adjustment to gross income is wrong because a deduction for foreign taxes is an itemized deduction, not a deduction for AGI. Treating them as nondeductible ignores both the credit and the deduction.
questions.explanationJa:
外国に所得税を支払った個人は、米国の連邦所得税から外国税額控除（§901、§904の限度あり）として差し引くか、代わりに項目別控除の税金（§164(a)(3)）として控除するかを選べる。挙げられた扱いの中では、連邦所得税からの税額控除が正しい。
2%フロアの項目別控除とするのは、税金はもともと2%の雑項目控除ではなく、その区分も現行法では認められないので誤り。AGI前の控除とするのは、外国税の控除は項目別控除であるため誤り。控除不可とするのは税額控除と所得控除の両方を無視している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.49

questions.stem: Carter incurred the following expenses in the current year: $500 for the preparation of a personal income tax return, $100 for custodial fees on an IRA, $150 for professional publications, and $2,000 for union dues. Carter's current year adjusted gross income is $75,000. Carter, who is not self-employed, itemizes deductions. What will Carter's deduction be for miscellaneous itemized deductions after any limitations in the current year?
questions.explanation:
Miscellaneous itemized deductions subject to the 2% of AGI floor (IRC §67) are not allowed for tax years after 2017; the TCJA suspension was made permanent by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (§67(g)). Tax return preparation fees, IRA custodial fees, professional publications for an employee, and union dues are all items in that category, and Carter is not self-employed, so none can be deducted on Schedule C.
Total of the expenses = $500 + $100 + $150 + $2,000 = $2,750, but the deduction allowed = $0
The $750 amount and the $1,250 amount apply the former 2% of AGI floor ($75,000 x 2% = $1,500) to some or all of the expenses. The $2,750 amount deducts all of the expenses without any limitation.
questions.explanationJa:
AGIの2%を足切りとする雑項目控除（§67）は2018年以降認められず、TCJAによる停止はOBBBAで恒久化された（§67(g)）。申告書作成費用、IRAの管理手数料、従業員の専門誌代、組合費はいずれもこの区分に当たり、Carterは自営業者ではないのでSchedule Cでも控除できない。
支出合計は$500 + $100 + $150 + $2,000 = $2,750だが、控除額は$0
$750と$1,250は旧法のAGIの2%（$75,000 × 2% = $1,500）の足切りを一部または全部の支出に当てはめた誤り。$2,750は制限なしで全額を控除している。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Individual Taxation Q.50

questions.stem:
Items 17 and 18 are based on the following:
On March 1, Year 7, Lois Wheat was bequeathed 1,000 shares of Lane Corp. common stock under the will of her uncle, Pat Prisy. Pat had paid $5,000 for the Lane stock in Year 2. Fair market value of the Lane stock on March 1, Year 7, the date of Pat's death, was $8,000 and had increased to $11,000 six months later. The executor of Pat's estate elected the alternate valuation date for estate tax purposes. Lois sold the Lane stock for $9,000 on May 1, Year 7, the date that the executor distributed the stock to her.

How much should Lois include in her individual income tax return for the inheritance of the 1,000 shares of Lane stock which she received from Pat's estate?
questions.explanation:
Gross income does not include the value of property acquired by bequest, devise, or inheritance (IRC §102(a)). Lois therefore includes $0 in income for the inheritance itself. Only a later sale produces income, measured by the difference between the amount realized and her §1014 basis.

The $5,000 amount is Pat's cost, the $8,000 amount is fair market value at the date of death, and the $11,000 amount is fair market value six months later; none of these is income to the heir, because inherited property is excluded from gross income.
questions.explanationJa:
遺贈・相続で取得した財産の価額は総所得に含めません（IRC §102(a)）。したがって Lois が相続そのものについて所得に含める額は $0 です。所得が生じるのは後に売却したときで、売却額と §1014 の取得価額との差額で測ります。

$5,000 は被相続人の取得原価、$8,000 は死亡日の時価、$11,000 は6か月後の時価で、いずれも相続人の所得にはなりません。
questions.source: Proactive REG テキスト Property Taxation Q.17

questions.stem: Hall was bequeathed 500 shares of common stock under his father's will. Hall's father had paid $2,500 for the stock ten years ago. Fair market value of the stock on February 1, Year 1, the date of his father's death, was $4,000 and had increased to $5,500 six months later. The executor of the estate elected the alternate valuation date for estate tax purposes. Hall sold the stock for $4,500 on June 1, Year 1, the date that the executor distributed the stock to him. How much income should Hall include in his individual income tax return for the inheritance of the 500 shares of stock which he received from his father's estate?
questions.explanation:
Property acquired by bequest, devise, or inheritance is excluded from gross income (IRC §102(a)). Hall includes $0 in income for the inheritance of the shares. (His sale on June 1 is a separate transaction: under the alternate valuation election the stock distributed within six months is valued at the June 1 distribution date, $4,500 (§2032(a)(1), §1014(a)), so the $4,500 sale produces no gain.)

The $5,500 amount is the value six months after death, the $4,000 amount is the date-of-death value, and the $2,500 amount is the father's cost; none of these is income to the heir, because inherited property is excluded from gross income.
